constructs.merged_construct: Le Chatelier RLHF: Equilibrium-Restoring KL Control under Reward Stress
constructs.cognitive_distance_note: PPO for RLHF is a policy-gradient/alignment method; Le Chatelier's principle (a chemical equilibrium shifting to counteract an applied stress) is physical chemistry; physiological negative feedback (homeostatic set-point regulation by sensor-effector loops) is mammalian physiology. A clipped policy objective, a reaction-equilibrium law, and a hormonal thermostat have no shared venue.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Treat the policy-versus-reference distribution as a chemical equilibrium 'reaction' whose position is measured by the KL divergence acting as a reaction quotient Q, and treat the reward gradient as an applied stress. Import Le Chatelier explicitly: the effective KL penalty coefficient beta is not fixed nor merely adapted toward a target KL, but is computed as a counteracting force proportional to the *rate of change* of Q under the current reward push (d KL/d step), so that whenever reward optimization rapidly displaces the equilibrium, the penalty rises to partially restore it, and relaxes when the push subsides. Wrap this in a physiological negative-feedback loop with an explicit set-point KL* and both proportional and integral terms (sensor = measured KL, effector = beta and the clip range epsilon), giving homeostatic regulation rather than the brittle fixed-clip of standard PPO. Reward-model over-optimization (Goodharting) is interpreted as the equilibrium being driven into an unphysical region; the integral term accumulates and clamps it. The result is RLHF whose distributional drift is self-limiting and self-restoring, reducing reward hacking without a hand-tuned KL schedule and with provable bounded steady-state KL error.

dirac.variables: pi_theta = current policy; pi_ref = frozen reference; Q_t = KL(pi_theta || pi_ref) measured on the current batch (the 'reaction quotient', a nonnegative scalar in nats); KL* = target/set-point KL; e_t = Q_t - KL* (set-point error); dQ_t = Q_t - Q_{t-1} (discrete rate of change of the quotient under the reward push); beta_t = KL penalty coefficient; eps_t = PPO clip range; g_t^R = reward-advantage gradient; I_t = integral accumulator sum_{s<=t} e_s; k_P, k_I, k_D = proportional/integral/derivative gains; A = anti-windup clamp on I_t.
dirac.update_rule:
Standard PPO objective L = E[min(r_t A_t, clip(r_t,1-eps_t,1+eps_t) A_t)] - beta_t * Q_t, where r_t is the importance ratio. Replace fixed/target-only beta with a PID controller carrying an explicit Le Chatelier derivative term:
  e_t = Q_t - KL*
  I_t = clip(I_{t-1} + e_t, -A, +A)            # integral, anti-windup
  beta_t = softplus( k_P*e_t + k_I*I_t + k_D*max(dQ_t,0) )   # derivative acts only on increases (the 'stress')
  eps_t = eps_0 / (1 + lambda*max(dQ_t,0))      # clip tightens when equilibrium is being displaced fast
The k_D*max(dQ_t,0) term is the imported Le Chatelier law: penalty force proportional to the RATE the reward push is displacing the distribution, not just the displacement. When dQ_t<=0 (relaxing back) the derivative term vanishes and beta decays toward the steady-state value set by k_P,k_I.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: RLHF/PPO training loop only — specifically the inner per-update computation of the KL-penalty coefficient and clip range, executed once per gradient step after Q_t is measured. No change to the reward model, sampler, or network architecture. Drop-in replacement for the existing adaptive-KL controller (e.g., the standard target-KL beta update).
dirac.cost: Negligible: stores 3 scalars (Q_{t-1}, I_t, beta_t) and computes O(1) extra arithmetic per step. Q_t is already computed by standard KL-penalized PPO, so no extra forward/backward passes. Memory overhead ~constant; compute overhead <0.01% of a step.
dirac.failure_conditions: (1) If k_D=0 it collapses exactly to standard PI adaptive-KL control (the only novel ingredient is the derivative/rate term). (2) Batch-to-batch KL estimate noise makes dQ_t dominated by sampling variance, so k_D amplifies noise and destabilizes beta — requires EMA-smoothing dQ_t, which adds lag and weakens the 'instant counteraction' claim. (3) If reward over-optimization is slow and monotone (low dQ but steadily rising Q), the derivative term is small and the integral term does all the work, again reducing to PI control. (4) On-policy KL and reward gradients can be aligned such that raising beta also lowers reward signal, stalling learning (over-damping) if gains are too high.

einstein.why_it_should_work: Le Chatelier / homeostatic negative feedback says a system at equilibrium subjected to a stress shifts to PARTIALLY counteract the stress at a rate matched to the perturbation rate. The transferable invariant is rate-matched restoring force: a controller that opposes change proportionally to how fast the change is happening suppresses transients (over-optimization spikes) faster than one that only opposes the accumulated displacement. Reward hacking is overwhelmingly a fast-onset transient (the policy lunges toward a reward-model exploit), so a derivative/anticipatory penalty should catch it before the integral term has accumulated.
einstein.thought_experiment: A reward model has a sharp exploitable spike (a phrase the RM over-rewards). Under fixed-beta PPO the policy rushes toward it; KL jumps in a few steps. Under pure target-KL (PI) control beta only rises after the integral of the error accumulates — several steps of damage. Under the Le Chatelier rate term, the very first large dQ immediately inflates beta and tightens the clip that same step, braking the lunge before the exploit is locked in.
einstein.key_prediction: At matched final reward, rate-controlled KL yields lower peak KL excursions and lower reward-model-vs-gold-reward divergence (less Goodharting) than target-KL adaptive control, without a hand-tuned KL schedule.
einstein.falsifier: Run PPO-RLHF with (a) fixed beta, (b) target-KL PI control, (c) full PID with the rate term, all gain-swept. If (c) shows no reduction in peak KL or in gold-reward degradation at equal proxy reward versus the best (b), and never beats (b) on the diversity/over-optimization frontier, the imported Le Chatelier dynamic adds nothing beyond PI control.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Augment KL-penalized PPO with a full PID controller on the policy-reference KL whose distinctive, non-standard ingredient is a Le Chatelier derivative term: the penalty coefficient and clip range respond to the RATE at which reward optimization is displacing the distribution (max(dKL/dstep,0)), not only to the displacement itself, giving anticipatory braking of over-optimization transients on top of the existing integral set-point regulation. Honestly, the proportional+integral part is just the known adaptive-KL controller; the only genuinely new mechanism is rate/derivative control, and its benefit hinges entirely on KL-transient onset being faster than the integral's response and on the per-batch KL estimate being clean enough that the derivative term tracks signal not sampling noise. If KL estimates are noisy or over-optimization is slow and monotone, it collapses to standard PI adaptive KL.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: TL;DR summarization or HH-helpfulness with a learned reward model and a held-out 'gold' reward (a stronger judge). Model: a 1.3B-2B policy (e.g., Pythia-1.4B) with frozen reference. Baselines it must beat: (i) best fixed-beta PPO, (ii) target-KL adaptive-beta PPO, both gain/schedule-swept. Metric: gold-reward at fixed proxy-reward (Goodhart gap), and peak/area-over-threshold of KL trajectory. Win condition: PID-with-rate Pareto-dominates target-KL on (gold-reward, proxy-reward) with no per-run KL schedule tuning.
constructs.self_distance_note: Moderately far from standard practice in framing (chemical-equilibrium / homeostasis language, explicit reaction-quotient analogy) but mechanically close: PI adaptive-KL control already exists in RLHF; adding a derivative term is a small, recognizable control-theory extension. The novelty is concentrated almost entirely in the rate/derivative term and its anti-windup integral, not in the architecture.

constructs.merged_construct: Somatic-Hypermutation Best-of-N: Affinity-Maturation Sampling with Clonal Selection

parents.name: Best-of-N Sampling (Inference-Time Scaling via Rejection Sampling)

constructs.cognitive_distance_note: Best-of-N inference-time sampling is an LLM test-time-compute method; somatic hypermutation (AID-driven targeted mutation of antibody variable regions at rates 10^5-fold above baseline) and clonal selection (antigen-driven proliferation of the highest-affinity B-cell clones in germinal centers) are immunology. A reward-ranked sampler, targeted antibody mutation, and germinal-center B-cell selection share no natural research overlap.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Turn flat best-of-N into an iterative affinity-maturation loop. Round 1: sample N candidate responses (the naive B-cell repertoire) and score them with a reward model/verifier (antigen affinity). Apply clonal selection: keep the top-k highest-affinity candidates and 'clonally expand' them by allocating more of next round's budget to their lineages in proportion to reward, exactly as high-affinity clones proliferate. Apply somatic hypermutation with targeting: rather than resampling whole responses, introduce a high local mutation rate only in the spans most responsible for affinity gain or loss (identified via token-level reward attribution or self-critique), echoing AID's targeting of the variable region's complementarity-determining hotspots while leaving the framework regions conserved. Iterate selection-then-hypermutation for several germinal-center 'cycles', with the mutation temperature decaying as affinity plateaus. The result is a test-time search that concentrates compute on promising lineages and edits precisely the decisive spans, achieving higher final reward at equal total samples than independent best-of-N, plus a record of which response regions drove the improvement.

dirac.variables: N = total sample budget per round; R = number of rounds (germinal-center cycles); s(y) = reward/verifier score of candidate y ('affinity'); k = number of survivors kept per round (clonal-selection top-k); b_i = next-round budget allocated to lineage i (clonal expansion), sum_i b_i = N; H(y) = set of high-saliency spans of y identified by token-level reward attribution or self-critique; T_r = mutation temperature at round r; m = local mutation/resample rate inside H; B = total samples over all rounds = N*R (held equal to flat best-of-N for fair comparison).
dirac.update_rule:
Round r=1: draw N i.i.d. samples (naive repertoire), score all.
Repeat for r=2..R:
  1. Selection: keep top-k by s(y).
  2. Clonal expansion: allocate next budget b_i = N * softmax_i(s(y_i)/tau_sel) so higher-affinity survivors spawn more children.
  3. Targeted hypermutation: for each survivor y_i, locate hotspot spans H(y_i) = top tokens by |d s / d token| (attribution) or self-critique flags. Generate each child by re-decoding ONLY tokens in H(y_i) with sampling temperature T_r (framework/non-hotspot tokens frozen, like conserved framework regions); produce b_i children.
  4. Anneal: T_{r+1} = T_r * gamma if max-affinity gain < delta (plateau), else hold.
Return argmax_y s(y) over all rounds. The two imported dynamics are: clonal selection = reward-proportional budget reallocation across lineages; somatic hypermutation = localized high-rate edits confined to attribution-identified hotspots.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Inference-time / test-time compute only. Wraps the decoder + a reward model/verifier; replaces flat best-of-N rejection sampling. Requires a token-attribution or self-critique signal to define hotspots (either gradient-based reward attribution, or an extra cheap LLM critique pass, or a prefix-swap ablation). No training changes.
dirac.cost: Same TOTAL forward samples B=N*R as flat best-of-N IF children only re-decode the suffix from the first hotspot (partial regeneration reuses the shared prefix's KV cache), which is CHEAPER per child than a full sample. Overhead: (a) attribution — either ~1 extra critique pass per survivor (adds R*k passes) or backprop-based saliency (one backward per survivor); (b) bookkeeping of lineages. Net: modestly more compute per effective sample than naive BoN unless prefix reuse offsets the attribution cost; memory grows with k retained candidates + their KV caches.
dirac.failure_conditions: (1) If reward attribution is uninformative (hotspots ~ random spans), targeted mutation degenerates to random local resampling and the method approaches flat best-of-N with worse diversity. (2) If the reward model is exploitable, clonal expansion concentrates budget on a reward-hacking lineage and amplifies Goodharting (selection pressure toward the proxy's blind spots). (3) If gains come from GLOBAL restructuring (the right answer needs a different overall plan, not edited spans), freezing framework tokens prevents reaching it — local search trapped in a basin. (4) With k too small, premature convergence (loss of repertoire diversity); with k≈N it reduces to flat BoN. (5) Reward must be roughly decomposable to a span for attribution to mean anything; holistic rewards break the hotspot premise.

einstein.why_it_should_work: Affinity maturation is empirically one of the fastest known biological optimizers: it achieves 10^3-10^4 affinity gains in days by (a) NOT searching uniformly — it concentrates mutation on complementarity-determining hotspots while conserving the scaffold, and (b) reinvesting reproductive budget into the currently-best clones. The transferable invariant is sample-efficiency via targeted variation + selective amplification: under a fixed mutation budget, allocating variation to the dimensions that actually move fitness, and compute to the lineages already winning, beats uniform i.i.d. search. Flat best-of-N is uniform, memoryless search; this imports a search policy that biology evolved precisely because uniform search is too sample-expensive.
einstein.thought_experiment: A 200-token answer is correct except for one wrong arithmetic span. Flat best-of-N must re-roll the whole answer many times to randomly fix that span while keeping the rest right — exponentially unlikely. Affinity-maturation BoN identifies the bad span via attribution, freezes the correct 190 tokens, and hypermutates only the 10-token span, fixing it in a handful of children.
einstein.key_prediction: At equal total sampled tokens, iterative targeted affinity-maturation reaches strictly higher final best-of-N reward (and higher exact-match on tasks with localizable errors) than flat best-of-N, with the gap widening as answer length grows.
einstein.falsifier: On a task with localizable errors (e.g., multi-step arithmetic / code with one buggy line), if affinity-maturation BoN does NOT beat flat best-of-N at matched total token budget — or if ablating the hotspot-targeting (mutating random spans instead) leaves performance unchanged — then the imported hypermutation-targeting dynamic contributes nothing beyond ordinary iterative refinement.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Convert flat best-of-N into an iterative germinal-center search: each round keeps the top-k candidates, reallocates next-round sample budget toward higher-reward lineages (clonal selection), and generates children by re-decoding ONLY the attribution-identified high-saliency spans at elevated temperature while freezing the rest (targeted somatic hypermutation), with temperature annealing as reward plateaus. The win comes from sample-efficiency: targeted local variation plus selective amplification should beat memoryless uniform sampling whenever errors are localizable and the reward is attributable to spans. It is strongest on long, mostly-correct outputs with point defects and weakest (collapsing toward refinement-style baselines or even flat BoN) when attribution is uninformative, the reward is exploitable (clonal expansion then amplifies hacking), or the fix requires global restructuring that frozen framework tokens forbid.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: GSM8K or MBPP (errors are localizable). Model: a 7B base + a verifier/reward model (or unit-test pass-rate as the affinity signal). Baseline it must beat: flat best-of-N at the SAME total token budget, plus a control that does iterative resampling without hotspot targeting (random-span mutation). Metric: solve rate / pass@1-after-selection at matched total decoded tokens; report the budget at which it matches flat BoN's best score (sample-efficiency curve). Win condition: equal-or-fewer tokens for higher solve rate, AND the hotspot-targeted variant beats the random-span control.
constructs.self_distance_note: Conceptually distinctive (explicit clonal-selection budget dynamics + conserved-framework / mutated-hotspot decoding) but adjacent to a growing family of iterative-refinement and evolutionary test-time-search methods; the genuinely uncommon ingredient is attribution-confined partial re-decoding with reward-proportional lineage budgeting, rather than whole-sample resampling. Structurally it is an evolutionary search wrapper around a decoder, which is several steps removed from the standard single-shot rejection-sampling baseline.

constructs.merged_construct: Baroreflex Learning-Rate Control with Isostatic Slow-Rebound
constructs.cognitive_distance_note: Cardiovascular reflex arc (carotid-sinus stretch -> autonomic outflow) and viscoelastic crustal relaxation after ice unloading are textbook examples from cardiology and geophysics with zero literature overlap with adaptive gradient optimizers; neither would be reached by an optimization researcher.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Replace Adam's fixed scalar learning rate with a baroreflex set-point controller acting on the gradient-noise 'pressure' p_t = ||g_t||^2 / v_t (squared gradient over Adam's second moment). A fast afferent branch maps deviations p_t - p* into an immediate multiplicative correction on the step size eta_t <- eta_t * sigma(-k_baro (p_t - p*)), mimicking the sympathetic/parasympathetic push-pull that buffers blood pressure within heartbeats. Superposed is a slow isostatic-rebound channel: a second-order viscoelastic state r_t relaxes the set-point itself toward the long-run mean pressure with a Maxwell-body time constant tau >> 1, r_{t+1} = r_t + (1/tau)(EMA(p_t) - r_t), so p* = p*_0 + alpha r_t drifts only after sustained load changes (e.g., entering a sharp loss basin). The fast loop suppresses per-step instability while the slow loop prevents permanent over-damping, giving an optimizer that both reacts to acute gradient spikes and structurally 'rebounds' its aggressiveness once a difficult region is passed. New capability: automatic two-timescale step-size homeostasis without manual warmup/decay schedules.

dirac.variables: g_t = current gradient; v_t = Adam second moment (EMA of g_t^2); p_t = ||g_t||^2 / (sum v_t + eps) = scalar gradient-noise 'pressure'; p* = pressure set-point; k_baro = fast-loop gain; eta_t = effective learning-rate multiplier (fast, per-step); sigma = logistic squashing; r_t = slow viscoelastic isostatic state; tau = Maxwell relaxation time constant (tau >> 1, e.g. 10^3-10^4 steps); alpha = coupling of slow state into set-point; EMA(p_t) = slow exponential average of pressure; eta_0 = base learning rate.
dirac.update_rule:
Standard Adam: m_t, v_t EMAs; hat-update u_t = m_hat_t / (sqrt(v_hat_t)+eps).
Fast baroreflex loop (per step):
  p_t = ||g_t||^2 / (||v_t||_1 + eps)
  eta_t = eta_{t-1} * sigma( -k_baro * (p_t - p*) )      # high pressure -> shrink step (sympathetic withdrawal); low -> grow
  clip eta_t to [eta_min, eta_max]
Slow isostatic-rebound loop (set-point drifts after sustained load):
  P_bar_t = (1-rho) P_bar_{t-1} + rho * p_t              # slow EMA, small rho
  r_{t+1} = r_t + (1/tau) * (P_bar_t - r_t)              # first-order Maxwell relaxation toward long-run pressure
  p*_t = p*_0 + alpha * r_t                              # set-point rebounds only after persistent change
Parameter step: theta_{t+1} = theta_t - eta_0 * eta_t * u_t.
Two imported dynamics: fast logistic push-pull around a set-point (baroreflex) + slow second-order relaxation of the set-point itself (post-glacial rebound).
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Optimizer only. A wrapper around Adam that modulates the global (or per-parameter-group) learning-rate scalar each step using statistics Adam already maintains (g_t, v_t). Replaces external warmup/cosine/decay schedules. No model or data changes; integrates at the optimizer.step() level.
dirac.cost: Tiny. p_t needs ||g_t||^2 (one reduction, often already available) and ||v_t||_1 (one reduction). State: 3 extra scalars (eta_t, r_t, P_bar_t) globally, or per group. O(1) extra arithmetic per step beyond the two norm reductions; <1% overhead. Memory ~ number of parameter groups * 3 scalars.
dirac.failure_conditions: (1) If k_baro is small and tau->inf, both loops freeze and it reduces to constant-LR Adam. (2) The fast multiplicative law makes eta_t a product of logistics — it can ratchet (random-walk drift) if (p_t-p*) is biased; needs the slow loop or clipping to anchor it, else LR wanders. (3) p_t = ||g||^2/||v|| is near-constant at well-scaled Adam stationarity (numerator and denominator co-vary), so the control signal can be uninformative — the reflex barely fires. (4) Set-point chasing the long-run mean (r_t -> P_bar) can cancel the very deviations the fast loop should react to (the controller adapts away its own error), yielding no net regulation. (5) On problems where a tuned warmup+cosine schedule is near-optimal, the closed-loop schedule is unlikely to beat it and mainly removes tuning burden.

einstein.why_it_should_work: The baroreflex is a proven two-timescale homeostat: a fast neural arc buffers acute pressure transients within heartbeats, while slow effectors (and, by analogy, isostatic viscoelastic rebound) reset the operating point only after sustained load change — preventing the fast loop from fighting a permanent shift. The transferable invariant is separation of timescales in set-point regulation: react fast to transients, re-baseline slowly to regime changes. Optimization needs exactly this — suppress per-step gradient spikes (instability) WITHOUT permanently over-damping after the landscape changes (e.g., exiting a sharp basin). A single-timescale controller must trade these off; two coupled timescales need not.
einstein.thought_experiment: Training hits a sharp loss canyon: gradient norms spike. A fast reflex instantly shrinks the step, avoiding divergence. Once through the canyon, gradients stay moderate but the naive fast loop, having driven down LR, would keep it suppressed; the slow isostatic state then relaxes the set-point back up over ~tau steps, 'rebounding' aggressiveness so training doesn't crawl for the rest of the run.
einstein.key_prediction: With no warmup and no decay schedule, baroreflex+rebound Adam matches or beats tuned warmup+cosine Adam on final loss while showing fewer/no loss spikes, AND recovers (LR rebounds) faster after gradient-spike events than single-timescale adaptive-LR controllers.
einstein.falsifier: Ablate to one timescale: (a) fast loop only, (b) slow loop only, (c) both, vs tuned cosine. If 'both' never improves stability-vs-final-loss over the best single-timescale variant and over tuned cosine — or if disabling the slow rebound term changes nothing — the second (post-glacial) timescale is inert and the construct reduces to a one-loop adaptive LR.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Wrap Adam in a two-timescale closed-loop LR controller driven by a gradient-noise 'pressure' p=||g||^2/||v||: a fast logistic push-pull shrinks/grows the step to hold p near a set-point (baroreflex), while a slow first-order viscoelastic state relaxes the set-point itself toward the long-run pressure so the operating point re-baselines only after sustained regime changes (post-glacial rebound). The principled payoff is timescale separation — buffer transients fast, re-baseline slowly — which a single-loop adaptive LR cannot do simultaneously. Its main vulnerabilities: p_t can be near-constant at Adam stationarity (weak control signal), the multiplicative fast law can drift without the slow anchor, and the set-point relaxation can adapt away the error it is meant to correct; if any of these bite, it collapses to constant-LR or single-loop adaptive Adam, and on tasks where tuned cosine is near-optimal its value is mainly schedule-free convenience rather than a better optimum.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: train a small Transformer (e.g., ~50-125M params) on a language-modeling subset (WikiText-103 / a few hundred M tokens) OR a ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10. Baseline it must beat: well-tuned Adam/AdamW with warmup+cosine. Stress test: inject a phase that induces gradient spikes (curriculum jump, LR perturbation, or a sharp data-distribution shift). Metric: final validation loss/accuracy at matched compute, number of loss spikes / divergence events, and post-spike recovery speed of the LR. Win condition: equal-or-better final metric with NO hand-tuned schedule and demonstrably both timescales active (ablations of each timescale degrade results).
constructs.self_distance_note: Closed-loop learning-rate control exists in scattered forms, but the specific construction — a logistic baroreflex set-point on a gradient-noise pressure variable PLUS an explicit second-order viscoelastic (Maxwell/post-glacial) relaxation of the set-point as a distinct slow channel — is well outside standard optimizer design, which uses open-loop schedules or single-timescale adaptivity. The two-coupled-timescale homeostat framing is the structurally unusual element.

constructs.merged_construct: Frank-Starling Preload Gating for Mixture-of-Experts Capacity
constructs.cognitive_distance_note: The heart's length-tension autoregulation (greater filling -> greater stroke output) and the tropical Hadley overturning cell are cardiac physiology and climatology; sparse-MoE routing literature never references either.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Replace Switch Transformer's hard capacity factor with a Frank-Starling preload law per expert: an expert's effective compute output (its per-token gain) rises with its incoming token 'venous return' (assigned load) along a length-tension curve, so a transiently popular expert stretches and contracts harder (allocates more FLOPs/larger effective rank) up to a Starling plateau, after which further filling causes decompensation and the router sheds load — giving graceful, biologically-shaped overflow instead of a sharp drop. The Hadley cell provides the global redistribution circulation that closes the loop: tokens 'rise' at over-subscribed experts (the ITCZ), are transported aloft to under-utilized experts (descending subtropical branch) via an auxiliary meridional routing flow, and return along the surface, so the auxiliary balance loss is realized as a physical conserved circulation rather than a penalty term. Update: expert gain g_e = Starling(load_e) with refractory plateau; routing logits add a circulation potential that advects excess tokens down the utilization gradient. New capability: load-adaptive per-expert compute and self-balancing routing that maintains throughput under bursty token distributions.

dirac.variables: x = token hidden state; e = expert index; load_e = number/mass of tokens routed to expert e this batch ('venous return' / preload); g_e = Starling gain = per-token effective compute the expert applies (e.g., active rank, number of FLOPs, or width of a low-rank up-projection); L_plateau = Starling plateau (load beyond which gain stops rising / decompensates); router logits z_e(x); C_e = circulation potential added to logits to advect overflow; util_e = running utilization EMA of expert e; phi = utilization-gradient field driving the Hadley-like meridional flow; cap_e = soft per-expert capacity.
dirac.update_rule:
Frank-Starling preload law (per expert, per batch):
  g_e = g_min + (g_max - g_min) * Starling(load_e),  where Starling(L) = L/(L + L_half) for L <= L_plateau (rising length-tension limb), and Starling(L) decreases (decompensation) for L > L_plateau, e.g. multiply by exp(-(L-L_plateau)/L_decomp).
  Realize g_e concretely as effective rank: an expert with high g_e activates more of its low-rank columns / a wider FFN slice; low g_e activates fewer (a dynamically-sized FFN).
Hadley-cell redistribution (closes the load loop without a penalty term):
  Compute utilization gradient; over-subscribed experts (util_e high, the 'ITCZ') get a positive ascent; under-utilized get descent.
  Circulation potential C_e = -kappa * (util_e - mean_util)  added to router logits, so excess tokens are advected DOWN the utilization gradient to under-used experts; a fast 'jet-stream' channel can route a few high-salience tokens to any expert directly.
  Final routing: top-1 (Switch) over z_e(x) + C_e. The conserved meridional flow replaces the auxiliary load-balance loss with an explicit redistribution that conserves token mass.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Model architecture + forward pass of a sparse-MoE (Switch-style) layer: (a) the router (adds circulation potential to logits, replacing/augmenting the load-balance loss), and (b) each expert's compute path, which must support a variable, load-dependent effective rank/width (dynamic FFN). Training and inference both. Requires experts implemented to scale active capacity at runtime.
dirac.cost: Router overhead trivial (per-expert scalars: load_e, util_e, C_e). The real cost/benefit is variable per-expert compute: total FLOPs become data-dependent (busy experts spend more, idle experts less) — potentially lower average FLOPs under bursty loads, but it BREAKS the static, perfectly-batchable compute graph MoE relies on for efficiency, complicating kernel scheduling and capacity-factor memory pre-allocation. Variable rank means ragged tensors / masking. Memory must provision for g_max. Net: control logic cheap; systems-level batching cost potentially significant.
dirac.failure_conditions: (1) If g_e is forced constant (fixed FFN width), the Starling limb vanishes and the layer reduces to Switch + a circulation-based balance term ~ equivalent to existing auxiliary-loss balancing. (2) The decompensation (gain DROP past plateau) can starve a genuinely popular, important expert exactly when it is most needed — a self-inflicted bottleneck unless the plateau is set high enough that it never triggers (in which case it's just monotone saturating gain). (3) Circulation that advects tokens to under-used experts purely by utilization (not fit) routes tokens to wrong experts, hurting quality — same failure as overly strong load-balance losses. (4) On uniform (non-bursty) token distributions there is little overflow to redistribute and no preload variation, so the whole mechanism is dormant and matches Switch. (5) Variable-rank experts can destabilize training (capacity changing under the optimizer).

einstein.why_it_should_work: The Frank-Starling law is intrinsic autoregulation: the heart matches output to venous return beat-to-beat WITHOUT external neural command, because stroke volume rises with filling along a length-tension curve up to a limit. The transferable invariant is supply-following-demand via a local saturating gain, with a global conserved circulation that closes the loop. MoE's pathology is mismatch between a token's compute need (bursty, uneven demand) and the expert's fixed capacity, patched by a brittle hard capacity factor + a tuned auxiliary loss. Importing intrinsic length-tension autoregulation lets a transiently-popular expert do MORE work (graceful, demand-matched) instead of dropping tokens at a hard cliff, and the conserved meridional circulation balances load as a physical flow rather than a penalty knob — exactly the homeostatic 'match output to load' property the heart guarantees.
einstein.thought_experiment: A batch suddenly contains many tokens of one type (e.g., a burst of code). In Switch, the one relevant expert saturates its capacity factor and the surplus tokens are DROPPED (hard cliff, lost compute). Under Frank-Starling, that expert 'fills' more, raises its gain (activates more rank), and processes the burst with extra compute, while the Hadley circulation advects any true overflow to the nearest under-used compatible expert instead of discarding it.
einstein.key_prediction: Under bursty/non-stationary token distributions, Frank-Starling MoE has fewer dropped tokens and better quality-at-fixed-average-FLOPs than Switch with a tuned capacity factor + load-balance loss, with the advantage vanishing as the token distribution becomes uniform.
einstein.falsifier: Train Switch-MoE vs Frank-Starling MoE at matched average FLOPs on a workload with controllable burstiness. If, across burstiness levels, Frank-Starling never reduces token-drop rate or improves loss/quality over a tuned-capacity-factor Switch — or if the gain only ever sits on the saturating limb (decompensation never used and removable with no effect) — then the borrowed length-tension dynamic adds nothing beyond a dynamic-capacity Switch.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Replace Switch's hard capacity factor with intrinsic, demand-following expert autoregulation: each expert's effective compute (active rank/FFN width) rises with its assigned load along a saturating Frank-Starling length-tension curve up to a plateau, after which it decompensates and the router sheds load; a conserved Hadley-like meridional circulation potential advects overflow down the utilization gradient to under-used experts, replacing the auxiliary load-balance loss with a mass-conserving redistribution. The principled appeal is genuine: match supply to demand locally + balance globally by conserved flow, instead of a brittle cliff + tuned penalty. But the construct's value is gated by (a) the systems cost of data-dependent, ragged per-expert compute breaking MoE's batchable static graph, (b) decompensation risking self-starvation of important experts unless effectively disabled, and (c) circulation-by-utilization routing tokens to ill-fitting experts. If experts cannot vary capacity, it collapses to Switch + a circulation-flavored balance loss; on uniform loads it is dormant.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: language modeling with a small Switch-MoE (e.g., 8-16 experts, ~100-300M active params) trained on a corpus with engineered token-type burstiness (interleave domains in bursts). Baseline it must beat: Switch Transformer with tuned capacity factor + tuned load-balance loss, at matched average FLOPs. Metric: validation perplexity, token-drop rate, and expert-utilization variance, swept over burstiness. Win condition: lower drop rate and equal-or-better perplexity at matched average FLOPs under bursty regimes, with ablations showing both the variable-gain limb AND the circulation term contribute.
constructs.self_distance_note: Far from standard MoE practice on two axes: (1) variable per-expert compute via a physiologically-shaped saturating-then-decompensating gain (vs fixed expert width + hard capacity factor), and (2) replacing the auxiliary load-balance loss with a conserved advective circulation field. Dynamic-capacity routing and balance-loss-free routing each exist in isolated forms, but the cardiac length-tension + atmospheric-circulation framing and the explicit decompensation limb are structurally novel and cut against the static-graph efficiency assumptions of mainstream MoE.

constructs.cognitive_distance_note: The complement protein cascade (opsonization, membrane-attack amplification) and seismic-wave traveltime inversion belong to immunology and geophysics; speculative decoding for LLM inference shares neither.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Recast speculative decoding's accept/reject as a complement cascade. The draft model proposes K tokens; rather than a single rejection test, a sequential proteolytic cascade tags ('opsonizes') each draft token with escalating confidence fragments (C3b-like deposits) accumulated from cheap intermediate target-model signals (early-exit logits at successive layers), and a token is 'accepted' only once deposited confidence crosses a membrane-attack threshold, otherwise it is marked for phagocytic resampling. Amplification means one strongly-supported early token lowers the threshold for its successors (cascade gain), accepting long correct runs quickly. Seismology supplies a traveltime model that decides WHERE to spend full target-model passes: treating layer-wise logit changes as wavefronts, we invert for the 'hypocenter' depth at which the draft and target first diverge (analogous to locating an earthquake from P/S arrivals), and run the expensive full verification only from that depth onward, skipping shallow layers that already agree. Update: deposit c_i <- c_i + early_signal; accept when c_i > theta_MAC with neighbor-coupled threshold decay; verification depth = argmin of inverted divergence traveltime. New capability: graded, amplification-driven acceptance with depth-targeted verification, raising token acceptance length at lower verification FLOPs.

dirac.variables: Draft model q proposes K tokens y_1..y_K; target model p verifies; c_i = accumulated 'opsonin' confidence deposited on draft token i; theta_MAC = membrane-attack acceptance threshold; s_i^(l) = cheap intermediate target signal for token i at layer l (early-exit logit agreement / margin between draft token and target's early prediction); L = number of target layers, with a set of early-exit probe layers; gamma = neighbor-coupling cascade gain (an accepted high-confidence token lowers its successors' threshold); d* = inverted divergence depth (the layer from which draft and target first meaningfully disagree); w^(l) = wavefront/per-layer logit change used as 'arrival times' for the traveltime inversion.
dirac.update_rule:
Graded opsonization accept (replaces single accept/reject test):
  For token i, run target early-exit probes at increasing depths; deposit confidence:
    c_i <- c_i + s_i^(l)  for each probe layer l until c_i > theta_MAC (accept, 'MAC formed') or probes exhausted (-> resample / phagocytose).
  Cascade gain (neighbor coupling): if token i accepted with high c_i, lower successor threshold:
    theta_i+1 <- theta_MAC - gamma * max(c_i - theta_MAC, 0)   # long correct runs accept fast.
Depth-targeted verification (seismology traveltime inversion):
  Treat per-layer logit change w^(l) as wavefront 'arrivals'; invert for the divergence 'hypocenter' depth d* = argmin_l where draft and target predictions first separate (the layer where margin flips), analogous to locating a quake from P/S arrival times.
  Run the EXPENSIVE full target pass only for layers l >= d* (skip shallow layers that already agree across draft and target); shallow agreement is reused.
Final: accepted prefix = longest run with c_i>theta_i; on first rejection, resample that token from corrected distribution (as in standard speculative decoding) and continue.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Inference acceleration only — the verification step of speculative decoding. Replaces the exact accept/reject (which in standard speculative decoding requires a FULL target forward pass over all K draft tokens) with (a) graded acceptance from early-exit/intermediate target signals and (b) layer-skipping verification from divergence-depth estimation. Requires a target model with usable early-exit heads or intermediate logit lenses. Decoder-side; no training of the base models (early-exit heads may need light calibration).
dirac.cost: Goal is FEWER target FLOPs per verified token: accept easy tokens from shallow probes without the full depth, and skip shallow layers when verification is needed. Overheads: (a) early-exit/logit-lens projections at probe layers (small matmuls per probe), (b) the traveltime inversion (cheap argmin over per-layer margins), (c) extra logic/branching that harms GPU batching/parallelism. Risk: many small sequential probe steps replace one batched full pass, which can be SLOWER in wall-clock on GPUs despite fewer FLOPs. Memory: store per-layer probe logits.
dirac.failure_conditions: (1) CRITICAL correctness: standard speculative decoding is provably distribution-preserving because acceptance uses the EXACT target distribution. Accepting on early-exit/approximate signals breaks the exactness guarantee — the output distribution no longer equals the target's unless the graded test is constructed to be a valid sequential probability ratio test with correction; otherwise this is lossy/approximate decoding, not speculative decoding. (2) If early-exit signals are uninformative until the final layer (target only 'decides' late), d* ~ full depth and theta is reached only at the last probe — no FLOP savings, reduces to full verification. (3) Cascade gain (lowering successor thresholds) can accept an incorrect run once one token is over-confident — error propagation. (4) GPU under-utilization from sequential probing can erase FLOP savings in latency. (5) If draft and target diverge at shallow depth often, the skip-shallow-layers premise fails.

einstein.why_it_should_work: Two biological/physical invariants. Complement: graded, amplifying recognition is more efficient than a single all-or-nothing test — opsonization accumulates evidence and a strongly-tagged target lowers the bar for engaging neighbors (cascade gain), so obvious cases are resolved fast and cheaply while ambiguous ones get full escalation. Seismology: you can localize WHERE something happened (the hypocenter) from arrival-time differences without instrumenting everywhere — so you spend expensive measurement only where it matters. Transferred: verification effort should be GRADED (cheap evidence first, escalate only on doubt) and TARGETED IN DEPTH (full computation only from the layer where the draft and target actually start to disagree). Speculative decoding currently spends a full target pass on every drafted token regardless of how obviously right/wrong it is — both invariants say that is wasteful.
einstein.thought_experiment: The draft proposes a long, easy, high-probability continuation (e.g., boilerplate the target also strongly predicts). A shallow early-exit probe already agrees with high margin -> confidence crosses threshold immediately and, via cascade gain, the whole run is accepted without deep target layers. Only when the draft proposes a token the target's early layers are unsure about does verification descend to full depth — and only from the depth where disagreement emerges.
einstein.key_prediction: At matched output quality, graded/depth-targeted verification accepts equally long draft runs while using fewer target-model layer-FLOPs per accepted token than full-pass speculative decoding, especially on low-perplexity / boilerplate-heavy text.
einstein.falsifier: Measure accepted-tokens-per-target-FLOP and output quality vs standard exact speculative decoding. If graded verification cannot match the acceptance length at lower FLOPs without degrading output distribution (KL to target output rises), OR if removing depth-targeting (always verifying full depth) leaves FLOPs/acceptance unchanged, the imported cascade+traveltime dynamics add nothing over exact full-pass verification.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Replace speculative decoding's single exact accept/reject with graded acceptance: accumulate target confidence on each draft token from cheap early-exit/intermediate signals (opsonin deposition), accept once it crosses a threshold, and let a strongly-accepted token lower its successors' thresholds (cascade gain) so long correct runs clear fast; additionally, estimate the depth at which draft and target first diverge (a traveltime-style inversion over per-layer logit margins) and run full target verification only from that depth onward, skipping shallow layers that already agree. The efficiency logic is sound (grade effort to difficulty; compute deep only where needed). The decisive caveat: standard speculative decoding's correctness guarantee rests on using the EXACT target distribution for acceptance — accepting on approximate early signals turns this into LOSSY/approximate decoding unless the graded rule is engineered as a valid corrected sequential test, which then likely needs the late layers anyway. It collapses to full-pass verification whenever the target 'decides late' (uninformative early exits), and sequential probing can negate FLOP savings in GPU wall-clock.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: open-ended + boilerplate-heavy generation (e.g., code completion + Wikipedia continuation). Setup: a small draft model + a larger target model (e.g., 7B draft / 70B target, or 160M/1.4B for a cheap proxy) with early-exit logit-lens probes on the target. Baseline it must beat: standard exact speculative decoding (full-pass verification) at the SAME output quality. Metric: target layer-FLOPs per accepted token and mean accepted run length, PLUS KL divergence of generated-text distribution to the pure target model (to detect lossiness). Win condition: fewer target FLOPs per accepted token at negligible KL increase; report wall-clock to check the parallelism penalty.
constructs.self_distance_note: Far from standard speculative decoding, which treats verification as a single exact full-depth test with a hard correctness guarantee. The construct introduces (1) graded, evidence-accumulating acceptance with neighbor-coupled cascade gain and (2) depth-localized partial verification via an arrival-time inversion — both structurally alien to the exact-rejection-sampling formulation, and notably trading the method's signature distribution-exactness for approximate efficiency. Early-exit and layer-skipping exist separately, but the opsonization-cascade + seismic-hypocenter combination as a verification policy is well outside current practice.

constructs.merged_construct: Herd-Immunity Dropout with Seafloor-Spreading Capacity Accretion
constructs.cognitive_distance_note: The epidemiological herd-immunity threshold (1 - 1/R0) and mid-ocean-ridge crustal accretion are epidemiology and geology; standard regularization research on dropout draws on neither, and inverting dropout into a transmission-blocking constraint is non-obvious.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Invert dropout's constraint: instead of dropping units to prevent co-adaptation, treat over-reliance on a feature as a contagious pathogen and drop precisely enough units to push the network above a herd-immunity threshold that blocks 'transmission' of a single fragile feature through the layer. Each unit has an estimated reproduction number R0_i = expected number of downstream units whose activation collapses if unit i is corrupted (measured via a cheap perturbation probe); the per-layer keep-rate is set adaptively so the immune fraction exceeds 1 - 1/max_i R0_i, guaranteeing no single feature can drive a cascade of co-dependent activations — robustness as epidemic control rather than random masking. Seafloor spreading governs capacity growth: at a central 'ridge' (the most plastic layer) new units are accreted symmetrically over training and conveyed outward, aging as they migrate so older units become rigid (frozen) crust while fresh units near the ridge stay plastic, yielding a striped age structure that paces representational turnover. Update: keep_rate_l <- 1 - 1/R0_hat_l(t); new-unit spawn rate at ridge with magnetic-stripe-like freeze schedule by distance from ridge. New capability: targeted anti-fragility (provable block of single-feature cascade failure) plus controlled lifelong capacity expansion.

dirac.variables: Unit i in layer l; R0_i = estimated 'reproduction number' = expected number of downstream units whose activation changes by more than delta when unit i is corrupted (perturbation probe); keep_rate_l = per-layer probability a unit is kept (1 - dropout rate); herd threshold H_l = 1 - 1/max_i R0_i (immune fraction needed to block single-feature cascades); corruption probe = set unit i to baseline/noise and measure downstream activation collapse; ridge = the most plastic layer where new units are accreted; a_u = 'age' of unit u (steps since spawn / distance from ridge); freeze(a_u) = plasticity schedule decreasing with age; spawn_rate = rate of new-unit accretion at the ridge.
dirac.update_rule:
Herd-immunity adaptive dropout (per layer, periodically):
  Estimate R0_i for each unit via a cheap perturbation probe: corrupt unit i, count downstream units with |Delta act| > delta -> R0_hat_i. Aggregate R0_max,l = robust-max_i R0_hat_i (e.g., high percentile).
  Set drop fraction to exceed the herd threshold:
    keep_rate_l <- 1 - max(0, 1/R0_max,l + margin)   i.e. immune (dropped) fraction >= 1 - 1/R0_max,l
  Apply standard Bernoulli dropout at keep_rate_l during training; high-R0 (cascade-hub) units raise the required drop fraction for the layer, guaranteeing no single feature can drive a connected cascade.
Seafloor-spreading capacity accretion (lifelong growth):
  At the ridge layer, spawn new units at spawn_rate; assign age a_u=0.
  Each step, units 'migrate' (age increments); plasticity (effective learning rate / dropout exposure) follows freeze(a_u): near-ridge units stay plastic (high LR, normal dropout), old far units freeze (LR->0, kept), forming an age-striped structure (magnetic-stripe analogue).
  Net capacity grows but turnover is paced: youngest units learn new structure, oldest are rigid 'crust'.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Training-time regularization + (optionally) a growing-architecture schedule. The herd-immunity part is a drop-in replacement for fixed-rate dropout, computing per-layer keep-rates from periodic perturbation probes. The seafloor-spreading part modifies the architecture/optimizer: it adds units over training and applies an age-dependent plasticity (per-unit LR/freeze) schedule — relevant to continual/lifelong learning. Both are training-only; at inference dropout is off (standard) and the network is the accreted one.
dirac.cost: Herd part: perturbation probes are the cost — corrupting each unit and measuring downstream collapse is O(units) extra partial forward passes per estimation; amortized by estimating infrequently (every K steps) and on a subsample of units/batch. Memory: store R0_hat per unit (cheap). Seafloor part: growing parameter count (memory grows over training) + per-unit age and plasticity bookkeeping. Net: probe cost is the main overhead; can be made small via stochastic estimation but is strictly more than free fixed-rate dropout.
dirac.failure_conditions: (1) R0 (downstream collapse count) is essentially a sensitivity/influence measure; if estimated crudely it is noisy and the keep-rate becomes unstable. (2) The herd-immunity threshold 1-1/R0 assumes a branching-process/epidemic model of feature dependence (homogeneous mixing, single index case) that neural co-adaptation may not obey — the analogy may not yield the claimed cascade-blocking GUARANTEE; without that, it is just sensitivity-weighted adaptive dropout. (3) If all R0_i ~ 1 (no hub features), threshold -> 0, keep_rate -> 1, and it reduces to ~no dropout (or fixed-rate if margin added). (4) Dropping enough units to exceed a high-R0 threshold can be very aggressive, destroying needed capacity (the 'cure worse than disease'). (5) Seafloor accretion freezing old units risks loss of plasticity / capacity fragmentation; if the freeze schedule is wrong it either ossifies too early or never consolidates. (6) The two halves are loosely coupled — each could be evaluated independently.

einstein.why_it_should_work: Herd immunity gives a quantitative, threshold law: an epidemic on a network cannot sustain transmission once the immune fraction exceeds 1-1/R0, where R0 is the average secondary infections per case. The transferable invariant is a percolation/branching threshold for cascade containment: if 'fragile reliance on one feature' propagates like a contagion through co-dependent units, then immunizing (dropping) a computed fraction tied to the most contagious unit's R0 BLOCKS any single-feature cascade — turning robustness into an explicit threshold rather than a guessed dropout rate. Seafloor spreading supplies a separate invariant: ordered, age-structured turnover — new material forms at a ridge and ages/rigidifies as it migrates, giving a system that keeps a plastic frontier while preserving consolidated older structure (a natural answer to plasticity-vs-stability in lifelong learning).
einstein.thought_experiment: A layer has one 'hub' feature on which many downstream units co-depend (high R0); if that feature is noisy/spurious, corrupting it collapses a whole cluster (a cascade) — classic co-adaptation fragility. Fixed-rate dropout may not drop enough to break it. Herd-immunity dropout measures R0 for the hub, computes the immune fraction 1-1/R0, and drops at least that fraction, so during training the hub is reliably absent often enough that downstream units must develop redundant, non-co-adapted pathways — the cascade cannot persist.
einstein.key_prediction: Setting per-layer dropout from the measured 1-1/R0 threshold yields strictly better robustness to single-feature corruption / better generalization gap than the best fixed-rate dropout at matched average drop rate, with the advantage largest in layers that contain high-R0 hub features.
einstein.falsifier: Compare fixed-rate dropout (rate-swept) vs herd-immunity adaptive dropout at matched MEAN drop rate. If herd-immunity dropout does not improve robustness-to-feature-corruption or the generalization gap over the best fixed rate — or if measured R0 does not predict where dropout helps — then the epidemic-threshold law transfers no real structure beyond ordinary adaptive/sensitivity-based dropout. Separately, ablate seafloor accretion: if age-striped freezing gives no continual-learning benefit over a fixed network, that half is inert.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Set dropout adaptively per layer from a measured feature-dependency 'reproduction number': estimate, via perturbation probes, how many downstream units collapse when a unit is corrupted (R0_i), and drop at least the herd-immunity fraction 1-1/max_i R0_i, so no single feature can drive a co-adaptation cascade through the layer — robustness as epidemic control rather than a guessed rate; separately, grow capacity by accreting new plastic units at a 'ridge' layer that rigidify (freeze) as they age, giving age-structured turnover for lifelong learning. The cascade-blocking GUARANTEE is the strong claim and the weak point: it inherits the herd-immunity threshold only if neural co-adaptation actually behaves like a single-index branching process on a network, which is unverified — absent that, the method is sensitivity-weighted adaptive dropout (still possibly useful, but not a guarantee). It collapses to (near-)no-dropout when no hub features exist (all R0~1), and risks destroying capacity when R0 is large. The seafloor-spreading half is only loosely coupled and stands or falls on its own as an age-structured continual-learning schedule.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: image classification with strong overfitting pressure (CIFAR-10/100 with a moderately over-parameterized CNN, limited data) for the herd-immunity dropout; a class-incremental continual-learning benchmark (split-CIFAR / split-MNIST) for the seafloor-accretion half. Baseline it must beat: best fixed-rate dropout (rate-swept) at MATCHED mean drop rate, plus a sensitivity-weighted adaptive-dropout control to isolate the threshold law. Metric: test accuracy / generalization gap and robustness to targeted single-feature corruption; for continual learning, average accuracy and forgetting. Win condition: herd-immunity dropout beats fixed-rate AND the plain sensitivity-adaptive control at matched mean rate, and R0 predicts where it helps; seafloor accretion reduces forgetting vs a static net.
constructs.self_distance_note: Far from standard regularization practice, which uses a fixed or globally-tuned dropout rate with no per-unit dependency model. Casting co-adaptation as a contagion with an R0 and setting the drop fraction from the epidemic threshold 1-1/R0 is a structurally unusual, model-based inversion of dropout's purpose. The seafloor-spreading age-striped capacity accretion is a separate, also-uncommon growing/continual-learning schedule; the two are bolted together rather than mechanistically unified, so the construct is two distinct far-from-baseline ideas under one name.

constructs.merged_construct: Thermoregulatory Set-Point Temperature for Diffusion Sampling under Mantle-Plume Bursts
constructs.cognitive_distance_note: Hypothalamic thermostatic control of body temperature and buoyant thermal-diapir plumes detaching from the core-mantle boundary are physiology and geodynamics; DDPM noise scheduling is unrelated to either.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Import hypothalamic thermoregulation to make the diffusion sampler's effective temperature a regulated variable rather than a fixed schedule. A 'thermostat' tracks a proxy core temperature T_core (e.g., running estimate of score-field disagreement / local entropy of the denoiser) against a set-point; when sampling is 'overheating' (high-variance, mode-mixing region) the controller triggers heat-loss effectors — vasodilation/sweating analogues that raise the guidance strength and shrink the step (cooling toward the data manifold); when 'too cold' (over-confident, mode-collapsing) it triggers shivering — injecting extra Langevin noise to re-explore. Crucially the set-point itself can be transiently raised like a fever to escape spurious modes early in sampling, then lowered for sharp finishing. Mantle plumes model rare exploratory excursions: occasionally a buoyant 'thermal diapir' of elevated temperature detaches from a deep, stuck latent region and rises, locally and briefly re-noising a sub-region of the sample so a small patch can re-melt and recrystallize into a better local structure (decompression-melting analogue) without disturbing the converged remainder. Update: noise_scale_t and guidance_w_t = PID(T_core_t - setpoint_t); plume events sampled with low rate, applying localized re-noising to high-residual spatial blocks. New capability: self-regulating, fever-then-anneal sampling with targeted local refinement, improving sample diversity-fidelity trade-off without retuning the schedule.

dirac.variables: x_t = sample at diffusion step t (reverse process, t from T down to 0); s_theta(x_t,t) = learned score/eps prediction; T_core(t) = scalar 'core temperature' proxy estimated as a running normalized disagreement of the denoiser, e.g. T_core(t) = mean over a small ensemble or over MC-dropout of Var[s_theta(x_t,t)] divided by an EMA of that variance (so T_core ~ 1 at typical scale); H(t) = local predictive entropy proxy = -sum p log p over the per-pixel/per-patch softmax of a discretized denoiser head, optional alternative to variance; setpoint(t) = target value of the regulated proxy, a scheduled scalar in [setpoint_lo, setpoint_hi]; e(t) = setpoint(t) - T_core(t) = control error; w(t) = classifier-free-guidance scale; sigma(t) = injected Langevin/sampling noise scale (multiplier on the schedule's nominal sigma); k_P,k_I,k_D = PID gains; integ(t) = running integral of e; lambda_plume = per-step Poisson rate of a 'plume' event; B = a spatial block (patch) of the latent; resid(B) = local denoising residual norm on block B; rho = re-noise depth (number of forward steps applied locally during a plume).
dirac.update_rule: Baseline reverse step: x_{t-1} = mu_theta(x_t, t; w) + sigma(t)*z, z~N(0,I). REGULATOR: each step compute T_core(t); e=setpoint(t)-T_core(t); integ += e; w(t)=clip(w0 + k_P*(-e) + k_I*(-integ) + k_D*(-de/dt), w_lo, w_hi); sigma(t)=clip(sigma0(t)*exp(k_sig*e), sig_lo, sig_hi). Interpretation: overheating (T_core>setpoint => e<0) raises guidance and shrinks noise (cool toward manifold); too cold (e>0) raises sigma (shiver/explore). FEVER schedule: setpoint(t) starts high (setpoint_hi) for t in [T, 0.7T] then ramps to setpoint_lo for the final steps (explore-then-anneal). PLUME: with prob lambda_plume per step, pick the top-m blocks by resid(B); for each, apply local forward noising x_B <- sqrt(abar_{t+rho}/abar_t)*x_B + sqrt(1-abar_{t+rho}/abar_t)*eps to re-noise only block B by rho steps, then resume the global reverse process (decompression re-melt of a stuck patch). All else unchanged.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Pure inference-time sampler modification for a pretrained diffusion model (DDPM/DDIM/score-SDE). No retraining. Lives in the reverse-diffusion loop: T_core/H computed from forward passes of the same denoiser; w(t) feeds the existing CFG combination; sigma(t) feeds the existing stochastic update; plume is an extra localized forward-then-reverse on selected latent blocks.
dirac.cost: T_core via an ensemble of E denoiser evals costs E x forward passes per step (E=2-4 typical) OR ~free if estimated from CFG's already-computed conditional/unconditional pair disagreement (preferred: 0 extra passes, reuse ||eps_cond - eps_uncond||). PID/sigma updates are O(1) scalars. Plume events cost rho extra denoiser evals on the affected blocks at rate lambda_plume (set rate*rho*blocks << 1 step-equivalent). Net overhead 0-3x per-step compute depending on whether the CFG pair is reused; memory overhead negligible (a few scalars + the residual map already available).
dirac.failure_conditions: Collapses to baseline DDPM when (a) k_P=k_I=k_D=0 and sigma0,w0 fixed; (b) the disagreement proxy is uninformative (e.g. deterministic DDIM with E=1 and no MC-dropout makes T_core constant, killing the loop); (c) setpoint is flat and equals the natural operating point (no fever). Degrades below baseline if gains are too high (controller chases noise estimation jitter, inducing oscillatory guidance that over-saturates -> artifacts), or if plume re-noising fires on high-residual blocks that are legitimately detailed (re-melts good structure). Also reduces to known dynamic-guidance methods when only w(t) is varied on a fixed schedule (then it is CADS/annealed-guidance), so the load-bearing novelty is the closed-loop feedback on a measured proxy plus the localized plume.

einstein.why_it_should_work: Transferred invariant: homeostatic set-point regulation keeps a controlled variable near a reference despite disturbances by negative feedback on effectors, and the regulated variable (temperature) is decoupled from the raw drive. In diffusion, sample 'temperature' (entropy/variance of the trajectory) is the quantity that actually governs the diversity-fidelity trade-off; standard schedules set effectors (sigma, w) open-loop and therefore cannot hold the true regulated quantity constant across prompts/images of differing difficulty. Closing the loop on the measured proxy is the principled move physiology already validates: regulate the output, not the input.
einstein.thought_experiment: Sample from a 2D mixture-of-Gaussians toy diffusion. With fixed sigma/guidance, hard (closely-spaced) modes either collapse (too little exploration late) or smear (too much noise late). The thermostat measures trajectory variance, raises noise early to populate all modes (fever) then anneals, holding measured spread on a target curve. Prediction: equal-sample coverage of all modes with sharper final localization than any single fixed schedule.
einstein.key_prediction: At matched NFE, closed-loop temperature control improves the precision-recall (fidelity-diversity) frontier vs the best fixed CFG+sigma schedule, with the largest gain on prompts/images where per-step disagreement variance is most heterogeneous.
einstein.falsifier: If, across a sweep of PID gains and setpoint schedules, the achievable precision-recall frontier never strictly dominates the frontier obtained by sweeping fixed (w, sigma) pairs at equal NFE, the feedback adds nothing beyond open-loop tuning and the construct is refuted.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Run a pretrained diffusion sampler with the reverse loop wrapped in a homeostatic controller: estimate a scalar 'core temperature' from denoiser disagreement (reusing the CFG conditional/unconditional gap for zero extra cost), and use a PID law to drive guidance scale up and sampling noise down when overheating, and noise up when too cold, tracking a time-varying set-point that is deliberately raised early ('fever' to populate modes) and lowered for sharp finishing. Rare Poisson 'plume' events locally re-noise the highest-residual latent blocks by a few forward steps and let them recrystallize, refining stuck regions without disturbing the converged remainder. Honest scope: the variable-guidance-only special case overlaps with annealed/dynamic CFG (CADS-like) and the localized re-noising overlaps with SDEdit/inpainting-style partial diffusion; the genuinely new content is (i) closed-loop feedback on a *measured* trajectory-temperature proxy rather than an open-loop schedule, and (ii) coupling that controller to residual-targeted local plume refinement. If the proxy is uninformative or the loop is detuned, it provably reduces to baseline (gains -> 0).
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: class-conditional CIFAR-10 generation with a small pretrained DDPM (~35M params) and a 2D mixture-of-8-Gaussians toy. Baselines to beat: best fixed-(w,sigma) DDIM/DDPM schedule and an annealed-guidance (CADS-style) baseline, all at NFE=50. Metrics: FID and precision/recall (and on the toy, mode coverage + intra-mode variance). Test whether closed-loop control Pareto-dominates the fixed schedules at equal NFE; ablate the plume term separately to isolate its contribution.
constructs.self_distance_note: Diffusion sampling normally uses an open-loop, prompt-independent noise schedule and a fixed (or monotonically scheduled) guidance scale; closing a measured-temperature feedback loop with a fever set-point and stochastic localized re-melting is structurally distant from the standard fixed-schedule sampler, while remaining adjacent to existing dynamic-guidance and partial-re-noising techniques.

constructs.merged_construct: Wound-Healing Phased LoRA Adaptation with Glacier Accumulation-Ablation Budgeting
constructs.cognitive_distance_note: The ordered hemostasis-inflammation-proliferation-remodeling program of tissue repair and the accumulation-versus-ablation mass balance of glaciers are physiology and glaciology; parameter-efficient fine-tuning never models adaptation as a healing or mass-balance process.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Borrow wound healing's temporally phased dynamics to schedule LoRA adaptation. A fine-tuning 'injury' (large task loss on the frozen base) launches four phases on the adapter ranks: (1) hemostasis — immediately clamp/stabilize the most disrupted directions with a low-rank fibrin patch; (2) inflammation — recruit extra transient rank and high learning rate to clear large errors; (3) proliferation — granulation: grow new low-rank directions where residual error persists; (4) remodeling — slowly prune and re-align ranks (collagen cross-linking) into a compact final BA, raising effective adapter quality per parameter. Phase transitions are gated by error-clearance signals rather than fixed steps, so easy tasks heal fast and hard ones linger in proliferation. Glacier mass balance governs the total rank budget as a conserved 'ice' mass: accumulation adds rank where high task 'snowfall' (gradient flux) lands in the upper layers, ablation melts rank where it sits below an equilibrium-line altitude of utility; net mass balance keeps the adapter's parameter count near a target while letting rank flow from low-value to high-value layers like ice creep. Update: phase(t) advances on clearance thresholds; rank_l <- rank_l + accumulation_l - ablation_l with global mass conservation. New capability: self-sizing, wound-like LoRA that allocates capacity exactly where and when the task needs repair, at fixed average budget.

dirac.variables: For layer l, adapter update Delta W_l = B_l A_l with rank r_l; W0 = frozen base weights; phase(l,t) in {hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, remodeling}; L(t) = task loss; clearance signal c_l(t) = relative drop in per-layer contribution to loss over a window, e.g. c_l = (L_{t-w}-L_t)/max(L_{t-w}, eps) attributed to layer l via gradient-norm share; eta_l(t) = layer learning rate; r_max = hard per-layer cap; R_total = global rank budget (conserved 'ice mass'); accum_l(t) = accumulation = f_acc(gradient flux ||g_l||, depth weighting, residual error); abl_l(t) = ablation = f_abl(singular-value mass below utility threshold); ELA = 'equilibrium-line' utility threshold on singular values; importance(sigma) = per-direction utility score (e.g. |sigma_i * <grad, direction_i>|).
dirac.update_rule: PHASE MACHINE per layer, advanced by clearance not fixed steps. Hemostasis: freeze all but top-r0 directions of the current residual; eta low; clamp exploding directions (gradient clip on the adapter). Transition to Inflammation when residual error stabilizes (||g_l|| stops growing). Inflammation: r_l <- min(r_l + Delta_r, r_max) (recruit transient rank), eta_l high; run until c_l(t) > tau_clear (large errors cleared). Proliferation: keep eta moderate; GROW new directions where residual persists: add a column pair (b,a) initialized from the top residual-gradient singular vector whenever residual on l exceeds tau_gran; run until residual plateaus (dc_l/dt ~ 0). Remodeling: stop growth; iteratively PRUNE smallest-importance directions and re-orthonormalize (collagen cross-link): drop direction i if importance_i < ELA, decay eta. GLACIER BUDGET (global, every K steps): compute desired r_l* propto accum_l - abl_l; then PROJECT onto sum_l r_l = R_total by water-filling: rank flows from low-importance layers (ablate) to high-flux layers (accumulate) while holding the total fixed. Concretely: rank_l(t+1) = rank_l(t) + round(accum_l - abl_l), then renormalize so sum stays R_total (Hungarian/greedy transfer of integer rank units from lowest-importance owners to highest-demand requesters).
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (training time only). Replaces the static-rank LoRA configuration and its fixed schedule: rank allocation, per-layer learning rate, and direction add/drop are made dynamic and gated by error-clearance and a conserved global budget. Inference is unchanged (final B_l A_l is merged or kept as standard LoRA).
dirac.cost: Memory: bounded by r_max per layer transiently during inflammation/proliferation (peak > target average), so peak optimizer memory ~ (r_max/r_avg)x a fixed-rank baseline of size r_avg; steady state equals a fixed-budget LoRA of total rank R_total. Compute: clearance/importance probes need per-layer gradient-norm and a small SVD or randomized-SVD on B_l A_l every K steps (O(r_l^2 d) cheap since r small). Rank-transfer is an O(L log L) assignment. Net training overhead ~5-15% wall-clock; zero inference overhead.
dirac.failure_conditions: Reduces to standard fixed-rank LoRA if phase gates never trigger (e.g. clearance thresholds set so it sits in one phase) and accum=abl everywhere (no rank flow). Reduces to AdaLoRA-like importance pruning if only the remodeling/budget parts are active and phases are removed. Breaks when clearance signal is noisy (mis-attributed loss drops cause premature phase advance -> under-fitting) or when adding/dropping directions destabilizes optimization (re-orthonormalization mid-training perturbs Adam moments; must reset moments for changed directions). Mass conservation can starve a layer that genuinely needs rank if R_total is set too low (over-tight budget -> worse than a generous fixed rank).

einstein.why_it_should_work: Two transferred invariants. (1) Wound healing: repair is a *staged* program where each stage's exit is gated by completion of the previous (debride before you rebuild before you remodel); applying capacity in the wrong order wastes it. Mapping: spend high learning-rate/transient rank to clear large errors first, then grow structure only where residual persists, then compress. This is a curriculum over *capacity*, not data, justified because the loss landscape's needs change over adaptation. (2) Glacier mass balance: a conserved quantity redistributes by flowing from low-utility regions (ablation zone) to high-input regions (accumulation zone) under a transport law; this enforces that total parameter budget is honored while capacity migrates to where gradient 'snowfall' is heaviest, the optimal allocation under a fixed budget.
einstein.thought_experiment: Fine-tune on a task whose difficulty is concentrated in a few layers (e.g. a synthetic task solvable by rank-2 edits in layers 5-6 only). A uniform fixed-rank LoRA wastes rank on layers 1-4. The mass-balance budget should drain rank from the easy layers and pile it on 5-6; the phase machine should blow through hemostasis/inflammation quickly and spend its time in proliferation exactly there. Prediction: same final loss as a hand-tuned per-layer rank, reached automatically.
einstein.key_prediction: At a fixed total adapter parameter budget, phased+mass-balanced LoRA reaches a target validation loss in fewer steps and/or at lower final loss than uniform fixed-rank LoRA and matches or beats AdaLoRA, with measured rank concentrating on the empirically hardest layers.
einstein.falsifier: If, at equal total parameters and equal training budget, the dynamic scheme never beats a per-layer-rank LoRA tuned by a single grid search (and never beats AdaLoRA), and the learned rank distribution does not correlate with per-layer difficulty, the staging+budget machinery is inert and the construct collapses to existing adaptive-rank PEFT.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Make LoRA adaptation a staged, budget-conserving process. A four-phase state machine (stabilize -> clear large errors with transient extra rank and high LR -> grow new low-rank directions only where residual persists -> prune and re-orthonormalize) advances per layer when error-clearance signals fire, so easy layers finish fast and hard layers dwell in growth. Overlaid is a conserved global rank budget that every K steps transfers integer rank units from low-importance layers to high-gradient-flux layers (water-filling under a fixed total), like ice creeping from accumulation to ablation zones. Honest scope: the remodeling+budget half overlaps strongly with AdaLoRA (SVD-based importance pruning and dynamic rank), and curriculum-over-capacity ideas exist; the distinctive content is (i) error-clearance-gated *phase transitions* governing the order and aggressiveness of capacity application, and (ii) a strict conservation constraint that forces rank to flow between layers rather than grow freely. If gates never trigger or budget equals supply everywhere, it provably reduces to fixed-rank LoRA or to AdaLoRA. A practical caveat is that adding/dropping directions must reset the corresponding optimizer moments to avoid instability.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: instruction-tune a small LLM (Pythia-410M or GPT-2-medium) on a mixed-difficulty SFT set, plus a synthetic 'hard-layer-localized' probe task. Model size: 350-410M base, LoRA total budget fixed (e.g. equivalent of rank-8 on all attention projections). Baselines to beat: uniform fixed-rank LoRA at the same total params, and AdaLoRA at the same budget. Metrics: validation loss / task accuracy at matched parameter count and matched steps; plus measured per-layer rank vs per-layer difficulty correlation. Ablate phases-only and budget-only.
constructs.self_distance_note: Standard PEFT assigns a fixed rank per layer with a fixed LR schedule and never models adaptation as a staged repair program or as a conserved mass that migrates between layers; the explicit phase machine and conservation constraint are structurally distant from vanilla LoRA, though adjacent to importance-based adaptive-rank methods like AdaLoRA.

constructs.merged_construct: Gate-Control Pain Inhibition for Gradient Routing with River-Delta Distributary Sharding
constructs.cognitive_distance_note: Spinal dorsal-horn gating of nociceptive versus tactile fibers and avulsion-driven distributary channel switching at river deltas are neurophysiology and geomorphology; routing reasoning-vs-tool gradients to disjoint adapters has no connection to either.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Import gate-control theory to resolve DART's gradient interference between reasoning and tool-use tokens. Model each LoRA adapter's interneuron 'gate' in the dorsal horn: large-diameter (high-confidence reasoning) fiber activity closes the gate to small-diameter (noisy tool-use) nociceptive gradients, so when a token is confidently a reasoning token its gradient inhibits leakage of conflicting tool-use updates into the shared backbone, and vice versa, implementing soft, activity-dependent disjointness instead of hard token-type routing. The gate's inhibitory interneuron is a learned function of the two fiber inputs' relative magnitudes, giving descending top-down modulation (a controller can globally raise inhibition to favor one capability). River-delta dynamics govern how the disjoint update streams are sharded across adapter sub-channels over training: gradient 'sediment' deposits into distributary channels (rank subspaces); when a channel aggrades (saturates) an avulsion reroutes future updates to a new lower-resistance subspace, preventing any single adapter direction from silting up and spreading capacity into a fan of specialized distributaries. Update: gate g = sigma(k(|reason_grad| - |tool_grad|)); blocked-stream gradient scaled by (1-g); avulsion triggered when channel utilization > threshold, reallocating to least-used rank. New capability: continuous interference suppression with self-distributing adapter capacity, improving joint reasoning+tool-use without rigid token partitioning.

dirac.variables: Two gradient streams per shared parameter (or per shared subspace): g_R = gradient from reasoning tokens, g_T = gradient from tool-use tokens; |g_R|, |g_T| = their norms (per-parameter-group); g_R_hat, g_T_hat = unit directions; gate value g in [0,1] = inhibitory interneuron output; k = gate sharpness; d = descending top-down modulation bias (a controllable scalar that shifts which capability is favored); LoRA adapters A_reason, A_tool plus shared backbone theta; for delta sharding, rank subspaces (distributaries) S_1..S_C within an adapter, each with utilization u_c (running fraction of update energy deposited) and capacity cap_c; avulsion threshold tau_av.
dirac.update_rule: GATE (per shared parameter-group, per step): g = sigma(k*(|g_R| - |g_T|) + d). The 'large-fiber closes the gate' rule: when reasoning gradient dominates (|g_R|>|g_T|), g->1 and the tool-use contribution into the SHARED backbone is suppressed; symmetric when tool dominates. Combined shared-backbone update: g_shared = g * g_R + (1 - g) * g_T (a soft, magnitude-gated selection: the dominant, more-confident stream passes; the conflicting weaker stream is attenuated by factor (1-g) or g respectively). The capability-specific adapters always receive their own full gradient (g_R into A_reason, g_T into A_tool); only the SHARED path is gated. Optional projection: if cos(g_R_hat, g_T_hat) < 0 (true conflict), additionally remove the conflicting component (PCGrad-style) before gating, so the gate handles magnitude dominance and projection handles direction conflict.
