DELTA SHARDING: deposit each shared update into the currently-active distributary subspace S_c*; track u_c via EMA of deposited update energy; when u_{c*} > tau_av (channel aggrades/silts), trigger AVULSION: reroute subsequent updates to argmin_c u_c (least-used subspace), i.e. swap the active rank subspace, and slightly decay the saturated subspace's learning rate (delta growth into a fan of channels). Descending control: an outer scalar d can be set per-batch to globally bias the gate toward reasoning or tool-use.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Training-time gradient routing for multi-capability fine-tuning (DART-style joint reasoning + tool-use). Sits between backprop and the optimizer step on the *shared* parameters/adapters: it reweights/combines the two task-conditioned gradient streams and chooses which rank subspace receives the shared update. Token-type attribution (which tokens are reasoning vs tool) yields the two streams. Inference unchanged.
dirac.cost: Requires computing two gradient streams (forward/backward per token-type, or a single backward with token-type masks to split contributions) — up to ~2x backward cost if streams are computed separately, ~0 extra if split by masking within one backward. Gate is an elementwise sigmoid over parameter groups (group-wise norms): O(#groups). Avulsion bookkeeping is O(C) per step with C small (number of subspaces). Memory: store per-group norms and per-subspace utilization (negligible). Net overhead 0-100% backward depending on stream computation choice.
dirac.failure_conditions: Reduces to ordinary multi-task LoRA with hard token routing if k->inf (gate becomes a hard 0/1 selection = DART's existing disjoint routing) or k->0 (gate=0.5, plain averaging of streams = standard joint fine-tuning). The directional-conflict projection, if omitted, means the gate only handles magnitude imbalance and provides no benefit when |g_R|~|g_T| but directions conflict (the hardest case) — there it degenerates to averaging. Avulsion can thrash if tau_av is low (constant rerouting prevents any subspace from learning). If the two capabilities do not actually conflict (gradients aligned), the whole mechanism is a no-op overhead. Magnitude-based gating can also pick the *louder* but wrong stream when gradient norm is a poor proxy for correctness (e.g. noisy tool-use with large but uninformative gradients closes the gate spuriously).

einstein.why_it_should_work: Transferred invariant from gate-control theory: a shared channel under competing inputs benefits from *activity-dependent presynaptic inhibition* where the higher-priority/larger-fiber input gates out the conflicting lower-priority input, plus top-down descending modulation to set global priority. This is exactly the multi-task gradient-interference problem on a shared backbone: rather than statically partition parameters, gate the shared update by which task is currently 'speaking with confidence', allowing soft, dynamic, context-dependent disjointness. The river-delta invariant: when a transport channel saturates (aggrades), the optimal response is avulsion to a lower-resistance path, which spontaneously produces a space-filling fan; mapped to optimization, this spreads capacity across rank subspaces and prevents any single direction from saturating/silting (loss of plasticity).
einstein.thought_experiment: Train a tiny shared MLP on two tasks whose per-example gradients on the shared layer point in conflicting directions for ambiguous tokens but align elsewhere. Plain averaging cancels learning on conflict tokens. Magnitude-gated combination lets whichever task is locally confident make progress without the other erasing it; over examples both tasks get served on their own confident tokens. Prediction: higher joint accuracy than averaging and than hard split, specifically on the conflict-heavy token subset.
einstein.key_prediction: On joint reasoning+tool-use fine-tuning, magnitude-gated shared-gradient routing (with conflict projection) improves the Pareto frontier of (reasoning accuracy, tool-call accuracy) over both naive joint training and hard token-type routing, with the gain concentrated on examples that mix both token types.
einstein.falsifier: If, on a benchmark with measurable reasoning/tool gradient conflict, gated routing never beats the better of {hard token-type routing, PCGrad-style projection alone} on the joint frontier across a sweep of k and d, then the gate adds nothing beyond known gradient-surgery/routing, and avulsion can be falsified separately by showing no plasticity benefit vs fixed subspaces.

constructs.refined_mechanism: On the shared backbone of a multi-capability adapter setup, combine the two task-conditioned gradient streams (reasoning vs tool-use) with a soft, magnitude-dependent gate: g = sigma(k(|g_R|-|g_T|)+d), so the locally more-confident (larger-norm) stream passes into the shared weights while the conflicting weaker stream is attenuated, with a descending scalar d for global top-down priority and an optional PCGrad-style projection to handle direction (not just magnitude) conflict. Capability-specific adapters always receive their own full gradients; only the shared path is gated. A river-delta 'avulsion' rule reroutes shared updates to the least-used rank subspace whenever the active subspace saturates, spreading capacity across a fan of distributaries to preserve plasticity. Honest scope: hard-gate and zero-gate limits recover DART-style routing and plain averaging respectively, and the conflict-handling overlaps with PCGrad/gradient-surgery; the distinctive contributions are (i) *soft magnitude-gated* shared-stream selection with top-down modulation (continuous, activity-dependent disjointness rather than a hard partition) and (ii) saturation-triggered subspace re-routing for sustained plasticity. The main risk is that gradient magnitude is an imperfect proxy for correctness.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: fine-tune a small instruction model (Pythia-410M / 1B) on interleaved reasoning + tool-call data (e.g. GSM8K-with-calculator or a synthetic tool-use set) where many examples mix both token types. Baselines to beat: (a) naive joint LoRA (averaged gradients), (b) hard token-type routed adapters (DART-style), (c) PCGrad projection. Metric: joint (reasoning accuracy, tool-call exact-match) frontier, plus accuracy on the mixed-token subset specifically. Ablate gate-only, projection-only, and avulsion-only.
constructs.self_distance_note: Multi-task fine-tuning normally either averages gradients or hard-partitions parameters by token type; a continuous magnitude-gated presynaptic-inhibition law on the shared stream plus saturation-driven subspace avulsion is structurally distant from standard routing, while overlapping with the known family of gradient-conflict-resolution methods (gradient surgery).

constructs.merged_construct: Pharmacokinetic Compartment Decay for KV-Cache Eviction with Atmospheric-Circulation Token Transport

parents.name: Agent Memory Below the Prompt (Persistent Q4 KV Cache)

constructs.cognitive_distance_note: Multi-compartment absorption-distribution-metabolism-elimination drug kinetics and three-cell meridional atmospheric transport are pharmacology and meteorology; quantized persistent KV-cache management for edge agents references neither.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Borrow pharmacokinetics to govern which KV entries persist, demote in precision, or evict. Treat each cached token as a drug dose distributed across compartments of decreasing fidelity: central compartment = full-precision on-chip KV (high bioavailability), peripheral = Q4 on-disk KV, deep = compressed summary. Each token follows ADME: Absorption when first attended (entering central), Distribution as it equilibrates between central and peripheral compartments by rate constants k12/k21 set by recent attention mass, Metabolism as quantization noise accrues, and Elimination with a per-token half-life so rarely-attended tokens decay exponentially out of the cache; a 'therapeutic window' keeps total cache concentration within the device memory budget by adjusting clearance. Atmospheric circulation supplies the spatial transport law that moves tokens between compartments and across attention heads: a Hadley/Ferrel/Polar three-cell flow advects high-salience tokens 'upward' into the central compartment and subsides stale tokens, while a jet-stream-like fast channel teleports a few globally critical tokens directly to any head. Update: concentration C_token follows multi-compartment ODE with rate constants from attention; eviction when C < MEC; circulation potential reassigns compartment by salience gradient. New capability: principled, budget-respecting cache lifecycle with smooth precision demotion instead of hard eviction, extending effective context on memory-constrained edge agents.

dirac.variables: Per cached token i: C1_i = concentration in central compartment = amount/precision of its KV stored on-chip at full precision; C2_i = peripheral compartment = Q4 (4-bit) on-disk/off-chip KV; C3_i = deep compartment = compressed summary (e.g. token merged into a low-rank summary slot); k12,k21 = inter-compartment transfer rate constants (central<->peripheral); k23,k32 similarly; ke = elimination rate (eviction); t_half_i = ln2/ke_i = per-token half-life; a_i(t) = recent attention mass on token i (sum of attention weights received over a window) — the 'dosing'/uptake signal; MEC = minimum effective concentration (eviction threshold); budget = total device KV memory; salience_i = a circulation potential (e.g. EMA of attention mass + positional/sink bonus). Three-cell transport: Hadley/Ferrel/Polar zones partition tokens by salience band; jet = a small fast lane that can move a few critical tokens directly to any head's central store.
dirac.update_rule: Each token's mass evolves by a linear 3-compartment ODE (discretized per decode step): dC1/dt = uptake_i - (k12+ke1)*C1 + k21*C2 ; dC2/dt = k12*C1 - (k21+k23)*C2 + k32*C3 ; dC3/dt = k23*C2 - k32*C3. UPTAKE: uptake_i = kappa * a_i(t) (attention received this step re-doses the token into central). RATE CONSTANTS FROM ATTENTION: k21_i (peripheral->central, 'distribution back to high fidelity') increases with recent a_i; k12_i (central->peripheral demotion) increases when a_i is low — so frequently-attended tokens stay full precision, ignored tokens demote to Q4 then to summary. ELIMINATION: ke_i set so half-life is long for high-salience, short for stale; token is EVICTED when C1+C2+C3 < MEC. PRECISION = compartment: living in C1 => fp16 KV; in C2 => Q4 KV; in C3 => summary only (smooth demotion, not hard drop). BUDGET CONTROL (therapeutic window): a global clearance multiplier alpha scales all ke so that sum_i (memory of token i) <= budget (raise clearance when over budget, like dose adjustment to keep total concentration in-window). CIRCULATION: compute salience potential; advect tokens up the salience gradient into central (Hadley rising at high-salience 'ITCZ'), subside low-salience tokens to peripheral/deep; the jet lane promotes the top-j globally-critical tokens directly to central for all heads regardless of band.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Inference-time KV-cache management for long-context / memory-constrained (edge) decoding, on top of a persistent quantized KV cache. Replaces the cache's eviction + quantization policy: instead of hard top-k eviction or fixed sliding window, tokens flow through fidelity compartments and are evicted on a concentration threshold. Hooks the attention readout (to get a_i) and the cache store/quantize/evict path.
dirac.cost: State per token: 3 scalars (C1,C2,C3) + a few rate constants => O(context) extra scalars, tiny vs the KV tensors themselves. ODE step is O(context) cheap arithmetic per decode step (a 3x3 linear update per token, vectorized). Quantization demotion (fp16->Q4) and summary compression have their usual costs but are amortized and reduce total memory (the point). Net: small compute overhead; net MEMORY SAVINGS vs full-precision full-cache (that is the capability). The salience/circulation computation reuses attention weights already produced, so ~0 extra attention cost.
dirac.failure_conditions: Reduces to a standard recency/attention-score eviction policy (H2O-like) if there is effectively one fidelity level (no Q4/summary tiers) and elimination is just 'evict lowest attention' — then the PK dressing adds nothing. Reduces to a fixed sliding window if rate constants are constant and uptake ignored. Breaks when attention mass is a poor predictor of future need (a token never attended recently but suddenly required — e.g. a far-back fact in a needle task — gets demoted/evicted just before use => accuracy cliff, the classic eviction failure). The linear-ODE assumption (no saturable/Michaelis-Menten kinetics) means heavy-hitter tokens can monopolize the central compartment; without a saturating term the 'budget' is enforced only by the crude global clearance multiplier. Lossy summary (C3) is unrecoverable, so any token wrongly pushed to deep compartment is effectively lost.

einstein.why_it_should_work: Transferred invariant from pharmacokinetics: a substance distributed across compartments of differing accessibility, with first-order transfer and elimination, naturally yields a *graded, multi-timescale retention* where importance (re-dosing = attention) keeps a quantity in the high-availability compartment and disuse causes exponential washout — exactly the behavior you want for a memory hierarchy (keep hot data hot, let cold data decay gracefully through cheaper tiers rather than be deleted abruptly). The atmospheric-circulation invariant supplies a conserved transport that continuously moves high-salience mass 'up' to high fidelity and subsides stale mass, with a fast jet lane for a few globally critical items — giving smooth tier migration instead of binary keep/evict. The principled advantage over hard eviction is the *smoothness*: precision degrades continuously, so a mis-ranked token loses fidelity rather than being lost.
einstein.thought_experiment: Two-tier toy: a long-context model with a memory budget far below full cache, on a task with both recent-dependent and one far-back critical fact. Hard top-k eviction deletes the far-back fact once newer tokens dominate attention; the PK scheme demotes it to Q4 then summary (still partially present) and, because the summary retains a low-fidelity trace, the model can still recover it with degraded but nonzero accuracy. Prediction: graceful accuracy degradation with budget, vs a cliff for hard eviction, at equal memory.
einstein.key_prediction: At matched KV memory budget, compartmental precision-demotion eviction yields a flatter accuracy-vs-budget curve (especially fewer catastrophic long-range retrieval failures) than hard attention-score eviction (H2O-style) and fixed-window baselines.
einstein.falsifier: If, across long-context retrieval and summarization benchmarks at several fixed budgets, the compartmental scheme never improves the accuracy-vs-memory frontier over the best of {H2O/attention-score eviction, sliding window, uniform quantization}, then the multi-compartment+circulation machinery reduces to known eviction/quantization and is refuted.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Manage a persistent quantized KV cache as a multi-compartment pharmacokinetic system: each token's 'mass' flows between a full-precision on-chip central compartment, a Q4 peripheral compartment, and a compressed-summary deep compartment via first-order rate constants driven by recent attention mass (attention = re-dosing), with a per-token half-life governing exponential washout and eviction triggered only when total concentration drops below a minimum-effective threshold. A global clearance multiplier keeps total memory inside the device budget (therapeutic window), and an atmospheric-circulation potential advects high-salience tokens up to full precision while subsiding stale ones, with a jet lane that promotes a few globally critical tokens directly. The capability is graceful *precision demotion* (fp16 -> Q4 -> summary) instead of hard eviction. Honest scope: with a single tier and attention-score elimination this collapses to H2O-style heavy-hitter eviction, and the quantization tiers overlap with existing mixed-precision KV methods; the distinctive content is the continuous multi-tier fidelity decay governed by attention-driven kinetics plus a conserved salience transport, aimed at smoother degradation. Key risk: attention-recency is an imperfect predictor, so a far-back fact can be demoted just before it is needed, and summary demotion is lossy/unrecoverable; a saturating (Michaelis-Menten) term is advisable to stop heavy hitters monopolizing the central compartment.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: long-context retrieval (needle-in-a-haystack with one far-back fact) + long-document QA/summarization on a small long-context LLM (e.g. a 1-3B model with 32k context). Memory budget fixed well below full cache (e.g. keep-fraction 25-50%). Baselines to beat: H2O / attention-score eviction, fixed sliding window, and uniform Q4 of the whole cache, all at the same memory budget. Metric: task accuracy / ROUGE vs memory budget curve, with special attention to long-range retrieval failure rate. Ablate compartments-only vs circulation-only.
constructs.self_distance_note: KV-cache management standardly uses hard eviction (sliding window or heavy-hitter top-k) and at most uniform quantization; modeling each token as a dose flowing through fidelity compartments with attention-driven kinetics and a conserved salience circulation is structurally distant from those policies, while adjacent to existing attention-score eviction and mixed-precision KV work.

constructs.cognitive_distance_note: Sealed-bid mechanism design and sports seeding (sport/games branches) are unrelated to neural-network sparse routing; nobody designs MoE gating as a truthful auction with second-price clearing and bracket-style anti-collision seeding.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Replace the MoE softmax-top-K gate with a per-token sealed-bid auction: each expert e emits a learned scalar 'valuation' v_e(x) of the token (a cheap bilinear score against the token's hidden state), and the router treats experts as bidders competing for the right to process the token. The K experts with highest valuations win, but each winning expert's *dispatch weight* (and the gradient gain on its valuation head) is set by the (K+1)-th highest bid rather than its own bid — a Vickrey/second-price rule that removes the incentive for any expert to inflate its valuation, empirically reducing router 'overbidding' collapse where one expert grabs everything. Seeding is imported as a capacity constraint: experts carry a running seed (their recent win count) and the dispatch matrix is built so that the two highest-seeded experts cannot both be assigned to the same token unless no lower-seeded expert clears a reserve price, spreading load like a tournament bracket keeps top seeds apart. The reserve price acts as a learnable null-route threshold so low-information tokens go to a shared dense path. This augments routing and load-balancing (not reward modeling): the auxiliary load-balance loss is replaced by the auction's own truthfulness incentive plus a seed-decay term, giving a new capability — incentive-compatible, self-balancing expert selection that resists router degeneration without a tuned balance coefficient.

dirac.variables: Token hidden state x; experts e=1..E; learned valuation head v_e(x) = bilinear score u_e^T W x (cheap scalar 'bid'); sort bids descending: b_(1) >= b_(2) >= ... >= b_(E); winners = top-K by bid; for a winning expert w, p_w = dispatch weight (the coefficient multiplying expert w's output in the combine step); second-price clearing price for the K-winner case = b_(K+1) (the highest losing bid); reserve price r = learnable null-route threshold; seed_e = running win count EMA (recent share of tokens won); s* = seed-decay coefficient; combine output y = sum over winners w of p_w * Expert_w(x).
dirac.update_rule: GATE = sealed-bid auction per token. (1) Each expert emits bid b_e = v_e(x). (2) Winners = K experts with highest b_e that also exceed reserve r; if fewer than K exceed r, remaining capacity routes to a shared dense path (null route). (3) VICKREY DISPATCH WEIGHT: instead of softmax over winners' own bids, set each winner's dispatch weight from the *clearing price* = the (K+1)-th highest bid: e.g. p_w = softmax_w( b_(K+1) )-normalized, OR more precisely p_w proportional to a function of (b_w - b_(K+1)) but with the GRADIENT to the valuation head detached/scaled by b_(K+1) rather than b_w. Operationally: y = sum_w sg[alpha_w] * Expert_w(x), where alpha_w is computed from the second price and sg is a stop-gradient arrangement so the valuation head's training signal does not reward inflating one's own bid (truthfulness: an expert cannot increase its own dispatch weight by raising its bid, because the weight is pinned to the next bid). (4) SEEDING anti-collision: maintain seed_e; build dispatch so the two highest-seeded experts are not both assigned to the same token unless no lower-seeded expert clears reserve r — implemented as a per-token penalty added to bids of high-seed experts when a high-seed expert already won this token, spreading load like keeping top tournament seeds in separate brackets. (5) seed decay: seed_e <- (1-s*)*seed_e + s* * won_e. NO separate auxiliary load-balance loss; balance comes from truthful bids + seed penalty + reserve.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: MoE routing layer (architecture + training). Replaces (a) the softmax-top-K gate's weighting of selected experts and (b) the auxiliary load-balancing loss. Inference uses the same bid+second-price selection (deterministic given weights). It is a *routing/load-balancing* mechanism — it does not touch reward modeling or the experts' internal computation.
dirac.cost: Bids are a bilinear scalar per expert = same cost as the standard router's logits (O(E*d_model) per token) — negligible vs expert FLOPs. Second-price weighting needs the (K+1)-th order statistic, i.e. one extra partial sort element (already have it from top-K selection). Seed bookkeeping is O(E) per step. Memory: one seed scalar per expert. Net overhead ~0 vs standard top-K MoE; it removes the aux-loss hyperparameter.
dirac.failure_conditions: PRECISE DIFFERENCES FROM STANDARD: standard top-K MoE weights selected experts by softmax over their *own* gate logits and adds an auxiliary load-balance loss (importance + load) with a tuned coefficient; expert-choice routing instead lets each expert select its top tokens (guaranteeing balance by construction). Vickrey-gating keeps token-choice top-K but (i) sets dispatch weight from the (K+1)-th bid not the winner's own, and (ii) replaces the aux loss with seed penalty + reserve. FAILURES: (a) The Vickrey 'truthfulness' theorem requires that an agent's *allocation* be independent of its own report given it wins and that its payoff be value-minus-clearing-price; here the 'expert' is not a self-interested utility-maximizer with a private fixed value — it is a trained head optimizing the *task loss*, so the auction's incentive-compatibility does not literally bind. The mechanism therefore reduces to: 'weight winners by the runner-up bid + stop-gradient on own-bid inflation.' That gradient-detachment is the only real effect; if sg is removed, it collapses toward standard softmax weighting. (b) If K+1 > number of bidders above reserve, clearing price is undefined -> must fall back. (c) Seeding can over-spread load and route tokens to poorly-matched experts (hurting quality) if the seed penalty is too strong — same risk as an over-weighted aux loss. (d) Pinning dispatch weight to b_(K+1) makes the weight nearly identical across winners when bids cluster, washing out the gate's selectivity (a known issue: it can under-weight a clearly-best expert).

einstein.why_it_should_work: Transferred invariant: in a second-price (Vickrey) auction, truthful valuation is a dominant strategy because a bidder's payment/allocation does not depend on its own bid in a way it can game, eliminating the incentive to overbid. The hoped-for transfer: MoE routers suffer 'overbidding collapse' where one expert's gate logits run away and it grabs most tokens (rich-get-richer load imbalance). Decoupling an expert's *gain*/training signal from its own report removes the self-reinforcing incentive to inflate, analogous to how second-pricing removes overbidding. Seeding adds a tournament-bracket invariant: deliberately separating top performers spreads competition, mapping to anti-collision load spreading.
einstein.thought_experiment: Two experts, one slightly better-initialized. Under softmax-top-1 with weak balancing, the better expert wins more, gets more gradient, wins even more -> collapse. Under Vickrey weighting with gradient detached from own bid, the better expert cannot amplify its dispatch weight by simply scoring itself higher (weight tracks the loser's bid), slowing the runaway; the reserve+seed sends marginal tokens to the under-used expert. Prediction: more balanced expert utilization at equal quality, without tuning an aux-loss coefficient.
einstein.key_prediction: Vickrey-gated MoE achieves load balance (low max/mean expert load ratio, high expert utilization entropy) comparable to a tuned auxiliary-loss baseline while removing the aux-loss coefficient hyperparameter, at equal validation perplexity.
einstein.falsifier: If, controlling for quality (perplexity), Vickrey-gating yields worse or equal load balance than (i) standard top-K with a tuned aux loss and (ii) expert-choice routing, AND ablating the stop-gradient detachment leaves results unchanged, then the auction framing contributes nothing beyond existing balancing and the construct collapses to 'softmax top-K with a runner-up-pinned weight.'

constructs.refined_mechanism: Keep MoE token-choice top-K selection but change two things: (1) set each winning expert's dispatch weight (and crucially detach the valuation head's gradient toward its own bid) from the (K+1)-th highest bid — a second-price/Vickrey rule whose intended effect is to remove the self-reinforcing incentive for a router head to inflate its own score and thereby slow 'rich-get-richer' expert collapse; (2) replace the auxiliary load-balance loss with a learnable reserve price (null-route to a shared dense path for low-information tokens) plus a seed-decay penalty that spreads high-win-count experts apart like separating top tournament seeds. Honest scope and precise differences: standard top-K MoE weights selected experts by softmax over their own logits and adds a tuned aux load-balance loss; expert-choice routing guarantees balance by letting experts pick tokens. The Vickrey claim of 'incentive compatibility' does NOT literally hold here because experts are not self-interested agents with fixed private valuations — they are heads trained to minimize task loss — so the only mechanically real effect is the stop-gradient that prevents own-bid inflation; if that detachment is removed the method reverts to standard softmax-top-K. A genuine risk is that pinning weights to the runner-up bid washes out gate selectivity when bids cluster. The defensible, testable contribution is therefore: 'aux-loss-free balancing via reserve+seed penalty, with own-bid gradient detachment to resist router collapse.'
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: language modeling with a small MoE Transformer (e.g. 8 or 16 experts, ~125-350M active params) on a standard corpus (C4/OpenWebText subset). Baselines to beat: top-K softmax gate WITH a tuned auxiliary load-balance loss, and expert-choice routing. Metrics: validation perplexity AT MATCHED quality, plus load-balance metrics (max/mean tokens-per-expert, utilization entropy, fraction of dropped tokens). Critical ablations: (a) remove the stop-gradient on own bid, (b) remove seed penalty, (c) remove reserve — to isolate which component, if any, drives balance vs the aux-loss baseline.
constructs.self_distance_note: MoE routing standardly uses a softmax top-K gate weighted by experts' own logits plus a tuned auxiliary balance loss (or expert-choice); pricing dispatch weights by the runner-up bid with own-bid gradient detachment and a tournament-seeding anti-collision rule is structurally distant from that practice, though the load-balancing goal and the bias/reserve mechanisms are adjacent to existing loss-free and reserve-based balancing schemes.

constructs.cognitive_distance_note: Golf handicapping (equalizing players of unequal skill via score adjustment) and chess zugzwang (forced detrimental move) are sport/games equalization and tempo concepts; Switch Transformer top-1 routing and its capacity factor have no handicap-index adjustment or forced-suboptimal-assignment law.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Import golf's handicap law into Switch Transformer's top-1 router to control expert load, and use zugzwang to handle capacity overflow. Each expert maintains a 'handicap index' computed from its recent routing differential — roughly (recent-token-share minus fair-share), low-pass filtered like a golfer's index from recent score differentials. At routing time the raw gate logits are adjusted by subtracting each expert's course-scaled handicap (strong/over-subscribed experts are penalized so weaker/under-used experts become competitive for marginal tokens), exactly as a handicap lets unequal players compete on net score; this replaces the auxiliary load-balancing loss with a deterministic, interpretable per-step adjustment that needs no balancing coefficient. When an expert hits its capacity-factor limit and a token would normally be dropped, the router invokes a zugzwang rule: rather than silently dropping (a free 'pass'), it is *forced to move* the token to its best legal (non-full) expert even if that expert is a poor match, and the magnitude of the resulting routing mismatch is logged as a tempo penalty that further raises the saturated expert's next-step handicap. This is a routing / capacity-control mechanism (not reward modeling): the new capability is token-drop-free, self-equalizing sparse routing whose load behavior is governed by a transparent control law instead of an opaque tuned loss.

dirac.variables: Top-1 (Switch) router; experts e=1..E; raw gate logit l_e(x) for token x; H_e = expert handicap index = low-pass-filtered routing differential, H_e <- (1-rho)*H_e + rho*(share_e - 1/E), where share_e = fraction of recent tokens routed to e and 1/E = fair share; c = course-scaling coefficient (maps handicap to logit units); adjusted logit l_e'(x) = l_e(x) - c*H_e (over-subscribed experts get penalized, raising weaker experts for marginal tokens); capacity_factor C and per-expert capacity cap = C * tokens / E; overflow = token whose argmax expert is at capacity; zugzwang move = forced re-assignment of an overflow token to its best NON-FULL expert; mismatch magnitude m = l_top(x) - l_legal(x) = gap between the preferred (full) expert's logit and the best legal expert's logit (the 'tempo penalty'); beta = coefficient turning mismatch into extra handicap on the saturated expert.
dirac.update_rule: ROUTING (per token, top-1): (1) compute raw logits l_e(x). (2) HANDICAP ADJUSTMENT: l_e'(x) = l_e(x) - c*H_e for all e. (3) select e* = argmax_e l_e'(x). (4) If e* is below capacity, route there. (5) ZUGZWANG OVERFLOW: if e* is at capacity, DO NOT drop the token; instead route to e_legal = argmax over non-full experts of l_e'(x) ('forced to move'), and record tempo penalty m = l_{e*}(x) - l_{e_legal}(x). (6) HANDICAP UPDATE (per step): H_e <- (1-rho)*H_e + rho*(share_e - 1/E); additionally H_{e*} <- H_{e*} + beta * (sum of m over tokens that overflowed e*) — saturated experts accrue extra handicap so they are penalized harder next step. NO auxiliary load-balance loss term: balance is produced by the deterministic logit handicap + the forced-move feedback. The handicap is a bias on logits, updated from realized load, not via gradient on a loss.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Switch-Transformer-style top-1 MoE routing (architecture + training, also active at inference). Replaces (a) the auxiliary load-balance loss and (b) the token-dropping behavior at capacity overflow. The handicap is a per-expert scalar bias added to the gate logits; the zugzwang rule changes the overflow handler from 'drop' to 'forced best-legal reassignment.'
dirac.cost: Handicap is one scalar per expert; logit adjustment is an O(E) vector subtraction per token (negligible vs expert FLOPs). Forced-move on overflow needs, for overflowed tokens, an argmax over non-full experts = O(E) per overflow token (cheap; only overflow tokens pay it, and reassignment means more tokens are actually processed — slightly higher expert utilization/compute than a baseline that drops them). Memory: E scalars (H_e). Net overhead ~0 in routing compute; removes the aux-loss coefficient; may increase processed-token count (no drops) hence marginally more expert compute than a dropping baseline.
dirac.failure_conditions: PRECISE DIFFERENCES FROM STANDARD: standard Switch uses a softmax router + an auxiliary load-balance loss (coefficient-tuned) and DROPS tokens that overflow capacity. The handicap term l_e' = l_e - c*H_e is, mechanically, ALMOST IDENTICAL to the now-standard 'loss-free / auxiliary-loss-free load balancing' that adds a per-expert bias updated from load (e.g. DeepSeek-V3-style bias b_e adjusted up for under-used and down for over-used experts). So the handicap half is NOT novel relative to bias-based loss-free balancing; it is a re-derivation of it with a golf metaphor and a low-pass-filtered differential (essentially an integral controller on load, which is what those biases already are). The GENUINELY DIFFERENT piece is the ZUGZWANG no-drop rule: forced reassignment of overflow tokens to the best legal expert PLUS feeding the resulting mismatch back as extra handicap. FAILURES/COLLAPSE: (a) if c=0 and no zugzwang, pure Switch with drops; (b) if only the handicap bias is used, it reduces to existing loss-free bias balancing (no new capability); (c) forced reassignment can route tokens to genuinely bad experts, injecting noise/hurting quality precisely when load is most skewed (the worst time) — this is the cost standard methods avoid by dropping; (d) the mismatch->handicap feedback can over-penalize a hot expert and cause oscillation (load ping-pong) if beta is large; (e) at inference, forced moves make routing load-history-dependent (non-deterministic across batch orderings), which can hurt reproducibility.

einstein.why_it_should_work: Transferred invariants. Golf handicap: subtract a skill-based offset so unequal players compete on net score — mapped to MoE, subtract a load-based offset from strong/over-used experts so under-used experts win marginal tokens, equalizing utilization without a tuned loss. This is a control-law (integral-feedback) view of load balancing and is sound — indeed it is why bias-based loss-free balancing works. Zugzwang: in chess a player forced to move worsens their position; the analogy says 'never let an overflow be a free pass (a silent drop) — force a move and pay a tempo cost.' The principle transferred is that *making the cost of saturation explicit and feeding it back* tightens the control loop and converts dropped tokens (lost computation/information) into processed-but-penalized tokens, trading a little per-token quality for zero token loss and stronger balancing pressure.
einstein.thought_experiment: A Switch layer with one 'popular' expert that keeps hitting capacity. Standard Switch drops its overflow tokens (information lost) and nudges balance via the aux loss. Handicap+zugzwang: the popular expert's handicap rises (fewer marginal tokens routed to it), and the overflow tokens it does receive are forced to the next-best expert and processed, while the mismatch they incur further raises its handicap. Prediction: zero dropped tokens and faster convergence of load to uniform than the aux-loss baseline, at a small, bounded quality cost on the reassigned tokens.
einstein.key_prediction: Handicap+zugzwang routing achieves zero token drops and equal-or-better load balance than a tuned auxiliary-loss Switch at matched perplexity; and against pure bias-based loss-free balancing, the zugzwang no-drop rule specifically reduces the token-drop rate to zero with <=epsilon perplexity change.
einstein.falsifier: If the handicap bias alone matches a tuned aux loss (expected) but ADDING zugzwang does not reduce token drops without hurting quality — i.e. forced reassignment's quality cost outweighs the benefit of processing those tokens, so net perplexity is worse than a dropping baseline at equal balance — then the only novel element (zugzwang) is refuted and the construct reduces to known loss-free bias balancing.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Augment Switch top-1 routing with a per-expert 'handicap' bias subtracted from gate logits, where the handicap is a low-pass-filtered load differential (recent share minus fair share), penalizing over-subscribed experts so under-used experts win marginal tokens — and replace the auxiliary load-balance loss with this deterministic adjustment. On capacity overflow, replace token-dropping with a 'zugzwang' rule: force the token to its best non-full expert and feed the resulting routing mismatch (tempo penalty) back as extra handicap on the saturated expert. Honest scope and precise differences: the handicap-bias half is essentially a re-derivation of *auxiliary-loss-free / bias-based load balancing* (e.g. DeepSeek-V3-style per-expert bias updated from realized load — an integral controller on utilization); it is not novel relative to that line, only re-metaphorized. The genuinely distinct contribution is the no-drop zugzwang handler: forced best-legal reassignment plus mismatch feedback, which converts dropped tokens into processed-but-penalized tokens and adds balancing pressure. The real trade-off is that forced reassignment injects low-quality routing exactly when load is most skewed (the moment standard methods avoid by dropping), so the bet is that processing-with-mismatch beats dropping; large mismatch-feedback gain risks load oscillation, and forced moves make inference order-dependent.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: language modeling with a Switch-style top-1 MoE (e.g. 16-64 experts, capacity factor 1.0-1.25), small scale (~125-350M active). Baselines to beat: (a) Switch with a tuned auxiliary load-balance loss (with token dropping), and (b) auxiliary-loss-free bias balancing (DeepSeek-V3-style) with dropping. Metrics: validation perplexity, load-balance (max/mean per-expert load, utilization entropy), and crucially TOKEN-DROP RATE. Decisive ablation: handicap-only vs handicap+zugzwang, to test whether the no-drop rule reduces drops to zero without hurting perplexity (the only claim not already covered by bias balancing).
constructs.self_distance_note: Standard Switch routing balances load with a tuned auxiliary loss and drops overflow tokens; framing balance as a golf handicap is a metaphorical relabel of the now-standard bias-based loss-free balancing (structurally adjacent, low distance), whereas the zugzwang forced-no-drop reassignment with mismatch feedback is structurally distant from both standard practice and bias balancing.

constructs.cognitive_distance_note: Open-ocean Pacific navigation that advances a position fix from heading/speed/time and reframes the canoe as stationary while reference islands slide past has no contact with hardware-aware selective recurrences; the link is the shared structure of accumulating, then resetting, integration error.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Augment Mamba's selective state update by treating the recurrent state as a dead-reckoning position estimate that accrues drift over long sequences, and add an Etak-style moving-reference correction. Concretely, the input-dependent gate Delta is reinterpreted as a confidence-weighted step size: when the current token strongly matches a learned 'reference landmark' embedding (a small bank of anchor vectors), the model performs an Etak update that re-expresses the hidden state relative to the passing reference (a learned affine reset toward the anchor) instead of integrating blindly. Between landmarks the state integrates ordinary selective updates (pure dead reckoning), and a per-channel drift estimator tracks expected integration error growing as sqrt(steps). When accumulated drift exceeds a threshold the next landmark match triggers a stronger correction, mirroring how navigators take an etak-island bearing to cancel cumulative course error. This gives the SSM an explicit, cheap error-resetting mechanism for very long contexts where fixed-size recurrent memory otherwise degrades, without reintroducing quadratic attention.

dirac.variables: h_t in R^N = Mamba SSM hidden state at step t (per channel). x_t = input token projection. Delta_t = input-dependent discretization step (softplus of a linear map of x_t). A in R^{NxN} (diagonal, entries a_i < 0), B_t, C_t = selective SSM matrices. {m_j} (j=1..L) = small bank of L learned 'landmark/anchor' embeddings in R^d (d = model width), L ~ 8-64. s_t,j = cosine(proj(x_t), m_j) = landmark-match score; j* = argmax_j s_t,j; gate rho_t = sigma(kappa*(max_j s_t,j - tau_land)) in [0,1] = landmark-firing strength (kappa sharpness, tau_land threshold). R_j in R^{NxN}, b_j in R^N = learned affine reset target associated with landmark j (a 'reference anchor' in state space). drift_t in R_{>=0}^N = per-channel running drift estimate; theta_drift = drift threshold.
dirac.update_rule:
Baseline selective scan: h_t_raw = exp(Delta_t * A) (.) h_{t-1} + (Delta_t * B_t) * x_t ; y_t = C_t . h_t. Etak augmentation, applied after the raw step:
  drift_t = lambda*drift_{t-1} + (1-lambda)*||h_t_raw - exp(Delta_t*A)(.)h_{t-1}||  (proxy for integrated update magnitude; lambda~0.99)
  reset_strength_t = rho_t * clip(drift_t/theta_drift, 0, 1)   # only correct when (a) a landmark fires AND (b) accumulated drift is large
  h_t = (1 - reset_strength_t) (.) h_t_raw + reset_strength_t (.) (R_{j*} h_t_raw + b_{j*})
  on reset (reset_strength high): drift_t <- (1-reset_strength_t)*drift_t   # error is cancelled, mirroring an etak bearing fix
All of R_j, b_j, m_j, kappa, tau_land, theta_drift trained end-to-end by backprop. Affine reset is a convex blend, so it is a no-op when reset_strength_t=0.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Inside each Mamba/SSM mixer block, immediately after the selective state-space scan and before the C_t readout, as a per-channel post-scan corrector. Adds an anchor-memory bank as block parameters. Active in both training and inference; in inference it preserves O(1)-per-token recurrence (no attention reintroduced).
dirac.cost: Per token: L extra dot products of width d for landmark scoring (L*d MACs, L<=64) plus one NxN affine apply if R_j is full (N^2) or N if R_j diagonal (recommended). Memory: L anchor vectors (L*d) + L reset maps. Overhead < 3-5% of the SSM block FLOPs if R_j is diagonal; negligible KV-style memory growth (state stays fixed size). No quadratic term.
dirac.failure_conditions: Collapses to vanilla Mamba when (i) landmarks never fire (tau_land too high or no recurrent token pattern correlates with anchors), or (ii) R_j -> I, b_j -> 0 (learned identity reset). Crucially, the 'dead-reckoning drift' premise partially fails by construction: Mamba's A has Re(a_i)<0, so the homogeneous state DECAYS rather than random-walks; there is no unbounded sqrt(t) error to cancel for content far in the past — it is already forgotten. The mechanism therefore does NOT fix drift in the navigational sense; it adds a content-addressable affine register/reset (an associative landmark memory). It reduces to a gated associative-memory write/overwrite, which can help only when the task needs to RE-ANCHOR state to a previously seen reference (e.g., variable rebinding, long copy/induction), not generic long-range decay.

einstein.why_it_should_work: The transferred invariant from Pacific wayfinding is NOT 'integration error grows' (that is false for a contractive SSM); it is the etak idea of re-expressing state in a moving reference frame: position is periodically re-coordinatized relative to a passing known island rather than integrated blindly. The genuinely portable principle is frame re-anchoring — replacing accumulate-only dynamics with intermittent absolute fixes at recognizable landmarks. In an SSM this maps to: when a token is recognized as a known referent, snap the latent to the canonical coordinates for that referent. This injects an absolute (content-addressed) correction into an otherwise relative (recurrent) estimator, which is exactly how a Kalman filter uses sparse measurements to bound the error covariance of dead reckoning.
einstein.thought_experiment: Sequence of the form: define A := <long random payload>; ... thousands of distractor tokens ...; recall A. A contractive SSM forgets the payload (state decays); attention would retrieve it. Give the SSM one landmark anchor that fires on the token 'A'. On the first 'A' the reset WRITES the payload into a protected anchor-aligned subspace (b_{j*}); on the second 'A' it reads it back. The Etak filter should recover A; vanilla Mamba should not.
einstein.key_prediction: On a long-context variable-rebinding/copy task, the Etak filter matches attention-level recall at sequence lengths where vanilla Mamba's recall has decayed to chance, at O(1) per-token cost.
einstein.falsifier: If, after training, learned R_j ~ I and b_j ~ 0 (landmarks add nothing) AND Etak gives no accuracy gain over a parameter-matched Mamba on rebinding/copy/induction tasks, the construct is refuted — it then is pure overhead and the 'navigation' framing carries no mechanism.

constructs.refined_mechanism: Stripped of the (incorrect) claim that a contractive SSM accumulates navigational drift, M035 is a gated, content-addressed affine reset of the Mamba state at learned landmark tokens — i.e., a small associative-memory register with overwrite/recall semantics bolted onto the selective scan. Its value, if any, is re-anchoring latent state to canonical coordinates for recurring referents, addressing SSMs' weakness at exact long-range retrieval and variable rebinding rather than at smooth long-range decay. It is closest in spirit to learned fast-weight/register tokens and to Kalman measurement updates over dead reckoning; the novel framing is making the reset fire on recognized landmarks and conditioning it on an integrated-magnitude proxy. Honest assessment: the drift-cancellation story is largely vestigial; the implementable, non-trivial part is the landmark-gated affine register.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: synthetic long-range associative recall + selective-copy (the standard Mamba probes) at lengths 2k-32k, plus a variable-rebinding task (bind k key->value pairs, query after N distractors). Model: 2-4 layer Mamba, ~5-20M params. Baseline to beat: parameter-matched vanilla Mamba (and a small attention model as an upper-bound oracle). Metric: exact-match recall accuracy vs sequence length, and FLOPs/token (must stay within 5% of Mamba). Success = recall curve shifted to substantially longer lengths at equal cost.
constructs.self_distance_note: Moderate-to-large structural distance: gated affine state resets and small anchor banks resemble fast-weights/registers and gated SSM variants, but conditioning the reset on landmark recognition plus an integrated-drift proxy, framed as moving-reference navigation, is not a standard SSM design pattern.

constructs.cognitive_distance_note: Christaller's settlement geography (threshold population, market range, hierarchical higher-order goods) and the Mongol yam relay spacing govern where towns and post-stations sit on a landscape; MoE routing is a learned sparse gate. Importing settlement-viability and relay-spacing laws as routing control is outside any human MoE intuition.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Govern MoE routing with central-place control laws instead of only a softmax gate plus load-balance loss. Each expert is a 'central place' with two imported parameters: a threshold (minimum routed token mass per batch below which the expert is deemed non-viable and its capacity/learning-rate is shrunk or it is merged with a neighbor) and a range (a soft radius in router-embedding space beyond which tokens are not served by that expert, forcing distant tokens to higher-order experts). Experts are organized hierarchically as in central-place theory: many low-order experts handle common, low-threshold 'goods' (frequent token patterns) while a few high-order experts, placed to cover the embedding space like rare regional capitals, handle rare high-threshold patterns. The yam contributes a spacing constraint: expert centroids are regularized to a roughly uniform day-march separation in router space so coverage has no gaps or wasteful overlaps, and a token always reaches a serving expert within a bounded number of routing hops. This yields self-organizing, gap-free expert specialization with explicit viability and coverage guarantees, improving load balance and reducing dead/redundant experts versus auxiliary-loss balancing alone.

dirac.variables: E experts, each with a centroid c_e in R^d in router-embedding space (d = router dim). Token t has router embedding u_t = W_r * x_t. Standard gate logit: l_{t,e} = u_t . c_e (or -||u_t - c_e||^2 in the geometric form). Imported parameters per expert: threshold T_e (minimum routed token mass per batch for viability) and range_e (radius: tokens with ||u_t - c_e|| > range_e are not served by e). Order/rank o_e in {1..H} = hierarchy level (low-order = frequent goods, high-order = rare goods); experts of order o have larger range and larger T. m_e = sum over batch of dispatch weight to e = realized 'market mass'. d_min = target uniform centroid spacing ('yam day-march').
dirac.update_rule: Routing per token: candidate set S_t = { e : ||u_t - c_e|| <= range_{o_e} }. If S_t empty, escalate to next higher order until non-empty (bounded hops <= H). Within S_t, top-K by l_{t,e} as usual (softmax over S_t). Viability control (per batch/EMA): m_e_bar = EMA(m_e); if m_e_bar < T_{o_e}: shrink expert (lr_e *= gamma<1; or freeze; or, if persistently dead, MERGE into nearest higher-order neighbor: c_{neighbor} <- weighted mean, transfer remaining mass). Spacing regularizer added to loss: L_yam = sum_{e<e'} relu(d_min - ||c_e - c_{e'}||)^2 (repel centroids to ~uniform separation) + optional coverage term sum_t relu(min_e ||u_t-c_e|| - r_cover)^2 (penalize uncovered tokens). Hierarchy: assign o_e by a budget (e.g., E/2 order-1, E/4 order-2, ...); range_o and T_o scale geometrically with o. Total objective = task loss + L_yam + (NO separate load-balance loss; viability+range replace it) , optionally retain a small balance term.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Replaces the MoE gating/dispatch logic and the auxiliary load-balance loss at training time; adds a centroid-spacing regularizer and a periodic viability/merge bookkeeping step (between optimizer steps). Inference: routing is the range-constrained top-K, same FLOPs class as standard top-K MoE.
dirac.cost: Routing: computing range membership needs the same E dot products / distances as standard gating (negligible extra). L_yam is O(E^2) per update but E is small (<=hundreds) -> cheap, and can be subsampled. Merge/spawn events are rare bookkeeping. Memory: +2 scalars (T_e, range_e) and an order tag per expert. Essentially zero added inference cost vs standard top-K MoE.
dirac.failure_conditions: Reduces to standard top-K MoE when range_e -> infinity (no geographic constraint) and T_e -> 0 (no viability pruning); then only L_yam remains, which itself reduces to a centroid-diversity regularizer. Breaks if d (router dim) is high: in high dimensions a fixed 'range' radius is nearly all-or-nothing (concentration of measure makes pairwise distances uniform), so range gating becomes trivial or starves experts. The yam uniform-spacing prior is WRONG when the true token density is highly non-uniform (Christaller assumes an isotropic plain); forcing uniform spacing then misallocates experts away from dense regions. Hierarchy buys nothing if token-pattern frequency is flat.

einstein.why_it_should_work: Central-place theory's transferable invariant is the threshold-and-range viability law: a service point survives only if it captures enough demand (threshold) and serves only customers within its range, and unmet demand for rare goods is aggregated upward into fewer, larger central places. Transferred to MoE, this is an explicit demand-coverage account of specialization: experts should partition the token-demand manifold into non-overlapping market areas with guaranteed coverage and no non-viable (dead) experts — directly targeting MoE's two chronic pathologies, dead experts and redundant overlap, which load-balance losses address only indirectly. The yam relay invariant (bounded spacing => bounded hops to a station) transfers as a coverage guarantee: every token reaches a serving expert within a bounded number of hierarchy hops.
einstein.thought_experiment: A 2-D router space with two token clusters of very different frequency. Standard top-K + load-balance loss tends to either split experts evenly (starving the rare cluster of coverage) or collapse. Central-place geography places many low-order experts on the frequent cluster (low threshold met) and one high-order expert covering the rare cluster (its range reaches the sparse points, its threshold is set low enough to stay viable). Result: gap-free coverage with no dead experts.
einstein.key_prediction: At fixed expert count and FLOPs, central-place routing yields fewer dead experts (mass below threshold) and lower expert-redundancy (representational overlap) than top-K + auxiliary balance loss, at equal or better perplexity.
einstein.falsifier: If, sweeping range and threshold, the configuration that minimizes validation loss is exactly the degenerate one (range=inf, T=0) — i.e., the constraints only ever hurt — then the geographic priors add no value and it collapses to standard MoE.

constructs.refined_mechanism: M041 differs from standard top-K and expert-choice routing in three concrete ways: (1) hard RANGE gating — each expert serves only tokens inside a learned radius in router space, making the candidate set token-dependent and bounded, unlike global top-K over all experts; (2) a VIABILITY threshold that prunes/merges experts whose captured token mass falls below a level, replacing the soft auxiliary load-balance loss with an explicit demand-coverage criterion plus hierarchical escalation of rare tokens to higher-order experts; (3) a yam SPACING regularizer enforcing roughly uniform centroid separation for gap-free coverage. Versus expert-choice (experts pick their top tokens, guaranteeing balance), central-place instead guarantees COVERAGE and viability via geometry, and adds an explicit hierarchy of capacities. The risk is that in high-dimensional router spaces the range and uniform-spacing priors become vacuous or actively harmful; its credible value is as a structured, interpretable replacement for the balance loss that provably eliminates dead experts.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: character/byte-level language modeling or a synthetic mixture-of-tasks with known non-uniform pattern frequencies. Model: small MoE Transformer, 8-16 experts, ~30-100M params, top-2 baseline. Baseline to beat: top-2 MoE with standard auxiliary load-balance loss (and expert-choice as a second baseline). Metric: validation perplexity AND (a) fraction of dead experts (EMA mass < threshold), (b) expert-utilization entropy, (c) pairwise centroid/representation cosine (redundancy). Success = equal/better perplexity with strictly fewer dead/redundant experts and no tuned balance coefficient.
constructs.self_distance_note: Moderate distance from standard practice: range-gated candidate sets and viability-based merging resemble capacity factors, k-means-style routing, and expert pruning individually, but the unified threshold/range/hierarchy/spacing law imported from settlement geography (replacing the balance loss outright) is not a configuration MoE practitioners normally reach for.

constructs.merged_construct: Leitmotif Retrieval Tags: semantic-cell index keys that recur on referent salience
constructs.cognitive_distance_note: RAG is a dense-retriever-plus-generator pipeline; the leitmotif is a Wagnerian compositional device where a short musical cell tags a character/concept and recurs whenever the referent becomes relevant; deixis is the linguistic anchoring of meaning to a speaker-centered origo. Opera orchestration and vector retrieval are unrelated.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Transfer the leitmotif's structure into the RAG index: each stored document chunk is augmented not with a single dense vector but with a learned short 'motif' embedding bound to the salient entity/concept the chunk concerns, plus a deictic origo vector encoding the chunk's point-of-reference (who/when/where it speaks from). Retrieval fires a motif when its bound referent becomes active in the query state, the way a leitmotif sounds whenever its character becomes relevant even if off-stage: the retriever scores chunks by motif-to-active-entity match weighted by deictic compatibility (same speaker/time frame) rather than raw query-chunk cosine similarity alone. Concretely, an entity-tracking head maintains a running set of active referent motifs from the generated context; at each retrieval step the top-K is selected by max over active-motif inner products, so a referent introduced early keeps pulling its associated evidence forward across long generations. This gives entity-persistent, viewpoint-consistent retrieval and reduces the classic RAG failure of losing track of a referent mentioned many tokens earlier.

dirac.variables: Corpus chunks {c_i}. Standard dense vector v_i in R^d for chunk c_i. Added per chunk: a motif embedding mu_i in R^{d_m} bound to the chunk's salient entity/concept e(c_i), and a deictic origo vector omega_i in R^{d_o} encoding point-of-reference (speaker/time/place frame). Query/generation state at step s: active-referent set A_s = { (entity_a, motif vector phi_a) } maintained by an entity-tracking head over the generated context; current deictic frame psi_s. Scoring weights alpha (dense), beta (motif), gamma (deictic). MEC-style activation: motif fires for chunk i when max_{a in A_s} <mu_i, phi_a> exceeds a salience threshold.
dirac.update_rule:
Entity tracking: after each generated span, update A_s by extracting mentioned entities and binding/refreshing their motif vectors phi_a (EMA of contextual entity embedding); decay inactive entities' salience. Retrieval score per chunk at step s:
  score(i) = alpha * cos(q_s, v_i)                              # standard dense term
          + beta  * max_{a in A_s} sal_a * <mu_i, phi_a>        # leitmotif term: fires on active referent
          + gamma * compat(omega_i, psi_s)                      # deictic compatibility (same speaker/time frame)
Top-K = argmax_i score(i). sal_a = current salience (recency/centrality) of active referent a. Training: contrastive loss to make mu_i align with its bound entity's contextual embedding; entity-tracking head trained with auxiliary entity-linking/coref supervision; alpha,beta,gamma learned or validated. Index stores (v_i, mu_i, omega_i).
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: The retriever's scoring function and index, in a RAG pipeline; plus a lightweight entity-tracking head running on the generator's context to maintain A_s and psi_s. Invoked at every retrieval step during generation (not just once at the start), enabling referent-persistent re-retrieval across long outputs.
dirac.cost: Index memory: +d_m + d_o per chunk (e.g., +25-50% index size if d_m,d_o ~ d/4 each). Retrieval compute: motif term needs |A_s| inner products per candidate (or a second ANN index keyed on mu); deictic term is cheap. Entity-tracking head adds a small per-step pass over generated tokens. If implemented as a second motif ANN index, overhead is ~2x retrieval latency; with re-retrieval each step, total retrieval calls grow with generation length.
dirac.failure_conditions: Collapses to standard dense RAG when beta=gamma=0, or when the entity-tracking head is uninformative (A_s empty/noisy) so the motif term never fires usefully. Degrades when chunks have no single salient entity (motif binding ill-defined) or when deixis is irrelevant to the domain (gamma noise). The entity tracker is a failure bottleneck: coref/entity-linking errors propagate as mis-fired motifs, potentially pulling wrong evidence forward more persistently than a stateless retriever would. Re-retrieval each step can amplify an early entity-tracking error across the whole generation.

einstein.why_it_should_work: The transferable invariant from the leitmotif is referent-triggered recurrence: a bound tag re-sounds whenever its referent becomes salient, even when the referent is off-stage (not lexically present in the immediate window). In retrieval this corrects the central RAG failure that relevance is computed from the local query window only, so a referent introduced far earlier stops pulling its evidence. Binding a recurring key to a tracked entity makes retrieval STATE-dependent on the discourse's active referents rather than memoryless on the surface query — an associative, entity-indexed memory. Deixis adds the second invariant: meaning is anchored to a speaker-centered origo, so evidence from an incompatible viewpoint/time frame should be down-weighted, improving consistency.
einstein.thought_experiment: A long multi-document answer that introduces entity X in paragraph 1, then discusses unrelated material for many tokens, then must continue X's thread. Standard dense retrieval at the later step (query no longer mentions X) retrieves off-topic chunks. The leitmotif retriever keeps X in A_s; X's motif keeps scoring X-bound chunks high, pulling the right evidence forward exactly when X re-becomes salient.
einstein.key_prediction: On long-form, multi-entity generation, leitmotif retrieval reduces referent-drift errors (retrieving evidence for the wrong/earlier-dropped entity) and improves entity-consistency of the output vs dense RAG at equal K.
einstein.falsifier: If, on a benchmark with long-range entity threads, adding the motif+deixis terms does not improve retrieval recall-for-active-entity or output entity-consistency over a strong dense/hybrid baseline (and ablating the entity tracker changes nothing), the recurrence mechanism does not transfer.

constructs.refined_mechanism: M047 augments RAG with an entity-indexed associative memory: each chunk carries a motif key bound to its salient referent and a deictic origo vector, and retrieval scoring is made state-dependent on a running set of active referents maintained by an entity-tracking head, so evidence for an entity introduced far upstream keeps being pulled forward whenever that entity is salient. This is structurally close to known ideas — entity-centric / coref-aware retrieval, query expansion with discourse state, and conversational memory — but the specific combination (referent-triggered recurrence as the primary scoring signal, plus viewpoint/time deictic compatibility, with per-step re-retrieval) is a tighter, more principled framing of entity-persistent retrieval. Its effectiveness hinges entirely on the quality of the entity-tracking head, which is also its main failure mode. Honest note: with a perfect coref system this overlaps heavily with entity-graph RAG; the novel contribution is the salience-gated recurrence and deictic gating rather than a new retrieval substrate.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: long-form multi-entity QA or narrative continuation where multiple entities' threads interleave (e.g., a synthetic 'multi-character dossier' with planted long-range references, or a long-conversation QA set). Model: small retriever (e.g., a 100M-param dual encoder) + small generator; index ~10k-100k chunks. Baseline to beat: dense RAG and a BM25+dense hybrid at matched K. Metric: recall@K for evidence of the currently-active entity, plus output entity-consistency/factuality (and an ablation removing the entity tracker). Success = higher active-entity recall and consistency at equal K.
constructs.self_distance_note: Moderate distance: motif/origo augmentation echoes entity-centric and coref-aware retrieval, but treating retrieval keys as Wagnerian leitmotifs that recur on tracked referent salience, gated by deictic viewpoint, is a non-standard organizing principle for a RAG index.

constructs.merged_construct: Apophatic Routing: experts defined by elimination rather than selection
constructs.cognitive_distance_note: MoE routing is a sparse-activation architecture; apophatic (negative) theology defines the divine purely by systematically denying every positive attribute; Occam's razor is a parsimony heuristic. A method that knows God only by what He is not, and a top-K gating softmax, share nothing.
constructs.p1_mechanism: Invert the MoE gate from positive top-K selection to apophatic elimination. Instead of a router emitting affirmative scores and keeping the highest-K experts, train a 'negation head' that emits a denial score for each expert -- a calibrated probability that this expert is wrong for the token -- and the token is routed to the experts that survive after iteratively removing the most-confidently-denied ones, stopping when removing another would discard support (an Occam stopping rule that halts at the smallest surviving set still covering the token's predicted loss). The denial scores are supervised by per-expert counterfactual loss (the increase in loss when an expert is masked), so the head learns negative evidence directly. This addresses MoE's known router miscalibration and expert collapse: negative routing produces sharper specialization because experts are excluded for concrete reasons, and the parsimony stop adaptively varies the active-expert count per token (hard tokens keep more survivors) instead of a fixed K. Implementable as a drop-in replacement for the gating softmax plus an auxiliary counterfactual-loss target.

dirac.variables: E experts. Token hidden state x. Standard gate: positive logits l_e(x), keep top-K. Apophatic replacement: a NEGATION head emits a denial score n_e(x) in [0,1] = calibrated probability that expert e is WRONG for x (high = confidently exclude). Survivor set S starts as all E experts. Counterfactual loss target: Dloss_e(x) = L(x | mask expert e) - L(x | all) = increase in token loss when e is masked (>=0 if e helps; ~0 if e is useless). Occam stopping signal: predicted covered loss with current survivors; stop removing when the next removal would raise predicted loss by more than epsilon (i.e., would discard support). Final active count k(x) = |S| varies per token.
dirac.update_rule:
Routing (inference) per token:
  S <- {1..E}
  repeat: e_kill = argmax_{e in S} n_e(x)
          if removing e_kill is 'safe' (predicted loss increase < epsilon, estimated by a learned support head, OR n_{e_kill} > tau_deny): S <- S \ {e_kill}
          else: break
  until |S| <= K_max or no safe removal remains
  dispatch token to survivors S with weights = softmax over -n_e(x) (or renormalized positive affinity) for e in S.
Training of negation head: regress n_e(x) toward a target derived from counterfactual loss, e.g. target_e = sigmoid(-rho * Dloss_e(x)) so that experts whose masking barely changes loss get high denial. Counterfactual Dloss_e is estimated cheaply by periodic single-expert mask probes on a subset of tokens (not every token every step). Add a parsimony pressure: small penalty on E[k(x)] to bias toward smaller survivor sets. Calibration term (e.g., temperature scaling / proper scoring rule) on n_e to keep denial scores calibrated.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Drop-in replacement for the MoE gating softmax + auxiliary balance loss, plus an auxiliary counterfactual-loss supervision signal for the negation head. The iterative elimination runs at routing time in every MoE layer; counterfactual probes run intermittently during training.
dirac.cost: Routing: the elimination loop is up to E iterations of an argmax over a shrinking set (O(E) per token, vs O(E log K) for top-K) — modestly more router compute but E is small. The real cost is TRAINING: estimating counterfactual Dloss_e requires extra masked forward passes (one per probed expert per probed token); even subsampled this is a meaningful training overhead (e.g., +probe_fraction * E forward-FLOPs in the MoE layers). Inference dispatch FLOPs depend on average k(x): if parsimony keeps k small it can be CHEAPER than fixed top-K; if hard tokens keep many survivors it is more expensive and variable (load becomes data-dependent, complicating batching).
dirac.failure_conditions: Reduces to standard top-K when n_e(x) is a monotone decreasing function of the positive gate logit and the stopping rule fixes |S|=K (then 'eliminate all but top-K' == 'select top-K'). The construct is only non-trivial if negative evidence is NOT a simple negation of positive evidence — i.e., if 'confidently wrong' is learnable separately from 'low affinity'. Breaks if counterfactual loss is too noisy/expensive to estimate (single-expert masking interacts with other experts, so marginal Dloss is not additive). Variable per-token k(x) breaks static expert-capacity/batching assumptions, risking throughput loss. If calibration fails, the Occam stop mis-fires (over- or under-pruning).

einstein.why_it_should_work: Two transferable invariants. From apophatic theology: identification by systematic negation can be sharper than affirmation when the positive signal is ambiguous but exclusions are confident — eliminating what is definitely wrong narrows the set more reliably than ranking what might be right, which directly targets MoE router miscalibration (routers are notoriously bad at absolute affirmative scores). From Occam's razor: stop at the smallest hypothesis set that still explains the data — here, the smallest expert set that still covers the token's predicted loss, giving per-token adaptive sparsity instead of a fixed K. The mechanistic bite is supervising the router with COUNTERFACTUAL loss (true marginal value of each expert) rather than with an unsupervised affirmative gate, which is a genuinely different and arguably better training signal.
einstein.thought_experiment: A token that two experts can each handle well (ambiguous positive: both have high but similar affirmative logits) but for which three other experts are clearly catastrophic. Affirmative top-2 must gamble between the two good ones using noisy logits. Apophatic routing confidently eliminates the three bad experts (high denial, well-calibrated from their large positive Dloss-when-forced) and keeps both viable experts as survivors, deferring the ambiguous choice to a soft mix — fewer catastrophic mis-routes.
einstein.key_prediction: Apophatic routing lowers the rate of catastrophic mis-routing (tokens sent to an expert whose masking would have DECREASED loss) and yields better loss-vs-active-FLOPs (adaptive k) than fixed top-K at equal average compute.
einstein.falsifier: If a learned negation head, after training, is essentially a sign-flipped copy of the affirmative gate (rank correlation of n_e with -l_e near 1) AND apophatic routing gives no improvement in mis-route rate or loss-vs-FLOPs over top-K, then 'elimination' carries no information beyond selection and the construct collapses.

constructs.refined_mechanism: M049 differs from standard top-K and expert-choice routing in WHAT the router is trained on and HOW the active set is sized. Standard top-K selects the K experts with the highest affirmative gate logits (an unsupervised, miscalibration-prone score, fixed K). Apophatic routing instead (1) trains a negation head with explicit COUNTERFACTUAL supervision — each expert's denial target comes from the measured loss increase when that expert is masked, a direct estimate of marginal value rather than an emergent gate; and (2) sizes the active set by an Occam stopping rule, iteratively discarding the most-confidently-wrong experts until further removal would discard support, so k(x) adapts per token (hard tokens keep more survivors). The honest risk is that, unless 'confidently wrong' is genuinely separable from 'low affinity', the method degenerates to top-K; and counterfactual-loss estimation adds real training cost and noise (non-additive expert interactions). Its defensible novelty is the counterfactual training signal plus adaptive, parsimony-bounded active-expert counts — both aimed squarely at router calibration and expert collapse.
constructs.minimal_experiment: Task: language modeling on a small corpus with a synthetic mixture-of-skills where ground-truth expert relevance is known (so mis-routing is measurable). Model: 8-expert MoE Transformer, ~30-100M params, top-2 baseline. Baseline to beat: top-2 MoE with auxiliary balance loss (and expert-choice). Metric: (a) loss/perplexity at matched AVERAGE active experts, (b) catastrophic mis-route rate (fraction of tokens routed away from an expert with positive counterfactual value), (c) router calibration (denial-score reliability), (d) distribution of k(x). Success = lower mis-route rate and better loss-vs-active-FLOPs without a tuned balance coefficient.
constructs.self_distance_note: Large distance from standard practice: counterfactual-loss-supervised routing and elimination-with-Occam-stopping are well outside the affirmative top-K/expert-choice paradigm, though counterfactual expert valuation echoes leave-one-out / Shapley-style attribution and pruning literature.

constructs.cognitive_distance_note: A phase-locked loop (phase detector + loop filter + VCO that drives a controlled oscillator to track a reference's phase) and the centrifugal flyball governor are classical control electronics/mechanics; adaptive-moment optimization is an ML training algorithm. Distinct fields.
constructs.p1_mechanism: A PLL locks a local oscillator to a reference by detecting phase error and feeding it through a loop filter to steer the oscillator's frequency until phase-aligned; a centrifugal governor regulates speed by feeding back rotational state to throttle input. Import the PLL control law to govern the learning rate of Adam. Treat the optimizer's effective update frequency (how fast parameters oscillate, estimated from the sign-change rate / autocorrelation of recent gradients) as a VCO, and treat a target oscillation rate (set so updates neither thrash nor stall) as the reference phase. Replace the fixed or cosine learning-rate schedule with a phase detector that measures the lag between gradient direction changes and parameter updates, passing this error through a loop filter (a low-pass on the phase error) that continuously nudges the learning rate to lock the update dynamics onto the stable reference rhythm, damping the oscillatory thrash that fixed Adam exhibits near sharp minima. The governor adds a hard speed limit: if measured update 'rpm' exceeds a threshold, a flyball-style term throttles the global step size. The new capability is a self-synchronizing optimizer whose learning rate is a closed-loop control output locked to the loss landscape's local oscillation frequency, rather than an open-loop preset schedule.

dirac.variables: Per parameter (or per layer/global) gradient g_t. Adam moments: m_t = beta1 m_{t-1} + (1-beta1) g_t, v_t = beta2 v_{t-1} + (1-beta2) g_t^2. NEW phase observable: oscillation rate f_t = EMA of the sign-change indicator of successive gradients, f_t = (1-c) f_{t-1} + c * 1[sign(g_t) != sign(g_{t-1})] in [0,1] (fraction of steps where gradient flips sign; high f = thrashing, low f = steady descent). Reference target f* in (0,1) = desired flip rate (set so updates neither thrash near 1 nor stall near 0; e.g., f* ~ 0.2-0.35). Phase error phi_t = f_t - f* . Loop filter (PI): integrator z_t = z_{t-1} + Ki * phi_t; control u_t = Kp * phi_t + z_t. Learning rate (the 'VCO frequency'): eta_t = eta_base * exp(-u_t) (more flips -> phi>0 -> shrink lr; fewer flips -> grow lr). Governor (flyball) hard cap: if f_t > f_max, eta_t <- min(eta_t, eta_gov) (speed limiter).
dirac.update_rule:
Standard Adam step uses eta_t in place of fixed eta:
  observe g_t; update m_t, v_t; update sign-flip rate f_t.
  phi_t = f_t - f*;  z_t = clip(z_{t-1} + Ki*phi_t, z_min, z_max);  u_t = Kp*phi_t + z_t.
  eta_t = eta_base * exp(-u_t);  if f_t > f_max: eta_t = min(eta_t, eta_gov).   # governor
  theta_{t+1} = theta_t - eta_t * m_hat_t / (sqrt(v_hat_t) + eps).
f_t can be tracked per-parameter (vector eta_t) or globally (scalar eta_t). Kp, Ki, f*, c are the loop-filter hyperparameters; integrator clamp prevents windup. The controller REPLACES the LR schedule (no cosine/warmup); warmup can be emulated by initializing z_0 high (small lr) and letting the loop raise it.
dirac.where_it_plugs_in: Wraps the optimizer's learning-rate computation (Adam/AdamW). It is a closed-loop LR controller reading gradient sign-flip statistics each step and outputting eta_t; sits between gradient computation and the parameter update. No change to the model or loss.
dirac.cost: Per step: one extra sign comparison and a few scalar/vector EMAs and the PI update — O(#params) elementwise if per-parameter, negligible if global. Memory: +1-2 scalars per tracked unit (f_t, z_t, previous-sign bit). Overhead << Adam's own moment storage (which is already 2 buffers). Essentially free.
dirac.failure_conditions: Reduces toward plain Adam-with-fixed-lr when Kp=Ki=0 (open loop) or when phi_t hovers near 0. CRITICAL distinctions/failure points: (i) the sign-flip rate is a NOISY, mini-batch-stochastic observable — with small batches gradients flip sign from sampling noise, not landscape geometry, biasing f_t high and forcing spurious lr shrinkage; (ii) the control loop can oscillate or go unstable itself if Kp/Ki are mistuned (a controller for the optimizer adds its own stability problem), and integrator windup can lock lr too low/high; (iii) f* is a new hyperparameter that may be as sensitive as the schedule it replaces. If the true landscape needs monotone lr decay (e.g., for convergence proofs), holding f_t at a constant target prevents the lr->0 annealing needed for convergence in stochastic settings, so it may not converge as tightly as a decayed schedule.

einstein.why_it_should_work: The transferable invariant from the PLL is closed-loop frequency locking via a phase detector + loop filter: rather than presetting an oscillator's frequency open-loop, you measure phase/frequency error against a reference and feed it back to steer the oscillator to the right rhythm. Optimization HAS a measurable update rhythm — the rate at which the gradient changes sign indicates whether steps are overshooting (thrash, too-large lr) or crawling (too-small lr). PLL theory says: regulate that rhythm with feedback to a target, and you get a self-tuning lr without an open-loop schedule. The centrifugal-governor invariant adds a saturating speed limiter for stability. This is principled BECAUSE sign-change rate is a known, cheap proxy for being at the right step size relative to local curvature/noise.
einstein.thought_experiment: A 2-D quadratic with an ill-conditioned valley followed by a flat plateau.
